   225	## Default Entry: Parallel PR Review, Any Orchestrator (owner-directed 2026-07-17)
   226	
   227	Invoking this skill against a SET of open PRs ("review the open PRs",
   228	"drain the PR backlog") means: review them in parallel, land them serially —
   229	no topology decisions required from the invoker.
   230	
   231	1. **Enumerate targets**: open, non-draft PRs in scope (drafts stay out of
   232	   scope per the draft rule below). Detect stacks and cumulative-tower
   233	   branches first; stacked PRs review and land bottom-up as deltas, never in
   234	   parallel with each other.
   235	2. **One isolated worktree per PR.** Parallel reviews never share a
   236	   worktree or a checkout; shared worktrees race and have destroyed findings
   237	   in this repo's history.
   238	3. **One reviewer process per PR at a time**, applicable lenses combined
   239	   into a single pass (two for large diffs), findings written incrementally
   240	   to an untracked file in that PR's worktree, verdict line last. Freeze
   241	   the PR's original changed-file snapshot BEFORE creating the findings
   242	   file; the findings file and any reviewer scratch artifacts are named
   243	   scope exclusions — they never enter `files_to_review`, the changed-file
   244	   set, or any commit. This is
   245	   the budget-adapted default of the Reviewer Fanout section below: under
   246	   the shared-pool budget, cross-PR parallelism replaces per-lens
   247	   parallelism; full per-lens fanout inside one PR remains available in a
   248	   quiet pool, and every applicable lens must be explicitly covered either
   249	   way.
   250	4. **Concurrency budget (shared codex pool).** Reviewer processes share one
   251	   pool with the audit lane's auditor seats and judicial panels. Keep the
   252	   TOTAL concurrent codex processes across every lane at or under ~8-10
   253	   (measured 2026-07-17: ~18 concurrent processes collapsed audit-lane
   254	   throughput from 6-11 landed verdicts/hour to ~1 every 3 hours). When the
   255	   audit drain is running at 4+ seats, run at most 2-3 concurrent PR
   256	   reviewers; scale up only in a quiet pool.
   257	5. **Each worker lands its own PR, end to end.** Fix Policy fixes, the
   258	   focused confirmation round, the landing, and the close-with-provenance
   259	   are all the final steps of that PR's own worker — never a separate
   260	   lander and never turn-taking. Workers land the moment their
   261	   confirmation passes: `origin/main`'s push atomicity is the only
   262	   serializer, and a lost push race costs seconds (re-fetch, re-cherry-pick
   263	   through the fail-closed loop, re-push, generated outputs restored). A
   264	   conflict touching only `docs/audit/data/citation_graph_manifest.json`
   265	   is resolved by regenerating it from the landed tree
   266	   (`build_citation_graph.py` then `write_citation_graph_manifest.py`),
   267	   never by hand-merge; a manifest regeneration touches only that generated
   268	   acknowledgment surface, so it needs no new reviewer round — any OTHER
   269	   conflict fails the landing closed and returns the PR to its worker for
   270	   re-review on a rebased head. Generated-output restoration is a
   271	   COMMIT-time rule (see the audit-compatibility gate), not a landing-time
   272	   step: the commits being landed are already clean. The fail-closed
   273	   landing loop is, exactly:
   274	   ```bash
   275	   COMMITS=(<oldest-sha> ... <newest-sha>)  # the PR's commits, oldest first
   276	   landed=""
   277	   for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
   278	     git cherry-pick --abort >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   279	     if ! { git fetch -q origin && git checkout -q --detach origin/main; }; then
   280	       sleep 3; continue
   281	     fi
   282	     if ! git cherry-pick "${COMMITS[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   283	       conflicts="$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U)"
   284	       if [ "$conflicts" != "docs/audit/data/citation_graph_manifest.json" ]; then
   285	         git cherry-pick --abort >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   286	         echo "FAILED: source conflict; return the PR to its worker" >&2
   287	         exit 1
   288	       fi
   289	       if ! { python3 docs/audit/scripts/build_citation_graph.py >/dev/null \
   290	              && python3 docs/audit/scripts/write_citation_graph_manifest.py >/dev/null \
   291	              && git add docs/audit/data/citation_graph_manifest.json \
   292	              && GIT_EDITOR=true git cherry-pick --continue >/dev/null; }; then
   293	         sleep 3; continue
   294	       fi
   295	     fi
   296	     if git push -q origin HEAD:main; then
   297	       landed="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
   298	
   299	exec
   300	/bin/zsh -lc "sed -n '261,520p' /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md && sed -n '521,780p' /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md && sed -n '781,1040p' /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md" in /Users/jonBridger/Toy Physics/.claude/worktrees/quirky-wiles-92e3b4
   301	 succeeded in 0ms:
   302	       break
   303	     fi
   304	     sleep 3
   305	   done
   306	   if [ -z "$landed" ]; then
   307	     echo "FAILED: landing did not complete after 4 attempts" >&2
   308	     exit 1
   309	   fi
   310	   git fetch -q origin
   311	   if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$landed" origin/main; then
   312	     echo "FAILED: $landed not contained in origin/main" >&2
   313	     exit 1
   314	   fi
   315	   echo "LANDED $landed"
   316	   ```
   317	   Every step is conditioned; push success captures the landed sha; retry
   318	   exhaustion and non-containment both exit nonzero — the loop can never
   319	   report success without the landed sha verified inside `origin/main`.
   320	6. **Who may kick it off: any orchestrator** — any Claude tier, a codex
   321	   session, or a human. The orchestration is process: every finding and
   322	   every PASS/FAIL verdict comes from the configured reviewer model's seats,
   323	   the orchestrator fixes only per Fix Policy, and nothing lands without a
   324	   reviewer PASS on its final state. The orchestrator never self-certifies.
   325	   Substituting a different reviewer family for a round (for example a
   326	   fresh-context reviewer when the codex lane is unavailable) requires
   327	   explicit owner authorization for that episode and must be disclosed in
   328	   the PR's provenance comment.
   329	
   330	7. **Progress reports every 15 minutes.** While any slot is active, emit a
   331	   summary block to the operator surface at least every 15 minutes — never
   332	   silence for a long session: a per-PR table (PR number, phase — reviewing
   333	   round N / fixing / confirmation / landing / landed / closed-with-reason —
   334	   reviewer runtime, and the finding count so far read from that PR's
   335	   incremental findings file), landings so far with their main SHAs, the
   336	   remaining queue, and the current codex process count against the budget.
   337	   A session that stops early still emits a final block with the same
   338	   fields; the Final Report section below remains the full closing artifact.
   339	
   340	The single-PR procedure in the rest of this skill is the inner loop of each
   341	parallel slot; nothing below is weakened by running slots concurrently.

   343	## Author Pre-Flight (input hygiene)
   344	
   345	Authors are expected to run [`PREFLIGHT.md`](PREFLIGHT.md) before requesting
   346	review. The pre-flight is authoring discipline, not a gate: it grants no
   347	standing, replaces no reviewer lens, and its absence blocks nothing by
   348	itself — but a reviewer may cite a skipped pre-flight item as a finding when
   349	the defect it would have caught is present. Whether such findings are fixed
   350	in place or the branch is rejected follows the existing Fix Policy and
   351	close-with-reason path; the checklist adds no new disposition.

   368	   - `docs/CANONICAL_HARNESS_INDEX.md`
   369	   - `docs/audit/README.md`
   370	   - `docs/ai_methodology/skills/PRIMITIVE_REGISTRY_CHECK.md`
   371	   - `docs/audit/data/axiom_premise_nodes.json` and the source notes named by
   372	     relevant primitive nodes
   373	   - `docs/audit/data/premise_decision_history.json`
   374	   - `docs/publication/ci3_z3/` when publication-facing files changed
   375	   - `docs/publication/ci3_z3/USABLE_DERIVED_VALUES_INDEX.md` when
   376	     quantitative or imported-value claims changed
   377	2. Determine the base ref:
   378	   - prefer `origin/main` if present;
   379	   - otherwise use `main`;
   380	   - if the current branch is the base branch, use `HEAD~1`.
   381	3. Compute the review base with `git merge-base HEAD <base-ref>`.
   382	4. Build the original changed-file set from committed, staged, unstaged, and
   383	   untracked changes. Do not review outside this set except interacting files
   384	   that are also in this original set.
   385	5. Record whether the worktree was initially clean. If it was dirty, do not
   386	   auto-commit without explicit user permission unless the slash-command
   387	   invocation clearly requested commit-producing fixes.
   388	6. If the task is to review open/non-landed PRs, include all non-merged,
   389	   non-draft PRs in the requested scope except PRs the user explicitly
   390	   excluded. Draft PRs are out of scope: ignore them entirely and do not land
   391	   them unless the user explicitly asks to inspect a draft PR without landing
   392	   it. Closed-but-unmerged PR heads can be inspected with `gh pr view` and
   393	   `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:refs/tmp/pr-<N>`.
   394	
   395	Useful commands:
   396	
   397	```bash
   398	git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD
   399	git diff --name-only --cached
   400	git diff --name-only
   401	git ls-files --others --exclude-standard
   402	git diff <base>...HEAD -- <files>
   403	git diff --cached -- <files>
   404	git diff -- <files>
   405	```
   406	
   407	For untracked files, include their full content or a concise new-file summary
   408	in reviewer prompts.
   409	
   410	## Stale PR Integration Guard
   411	
   412	When landing one or more PRs, protect already-landed science before applying
   413	any branch content. A PR branch may be based before another PR just landed, so
   414	checking out whole files from that stale PR head can erase current-main source
   415	science in shared files.
   416	
   417	For every PR before integration:
   418	
   419	```bash
   420	git fetch origin main pull/<N>/head:refs/tmp/pr-<N>
   421	pr_base=$(git merge-base origin/main refs/tmp/pr-<N>)
   422	comm -12 \
   423	  <(git diff --name-only "$pr_base"..origin/main | sort) \
   424	  <(git diff --name-only "$pr_base"..refs/tmp/pr-<N> | sort)
   425	```
   426	
   427	If the overlap list is non-empty, or if earlier PRs have landed during the
   428	same review-loop run, do **not** run `git checkout refs/tmp/pr-<N> -- <file>`
   429	for those paths. Integrate the PR's delta against its merge base with a
   430	three-way patch, rebase/merge, or cherry-pick source commits, then resolve any
   431	conflicts by preserving both current-main science and the salvageable PR
   432	science:
   433	
   434	```bash
   435	git diff --binary "$pr_base"..refs/tmp/pr-<N> -- <source paths> > /tmp/pr<N>.patch
   436	git apply --3way /tmp/pr<N>.patch
   437	```
   438	
   439	Whole-file checkout from a PR head is allowed only when the file is new on the
   440	PR or when `git diff --quiet "$pr_base"..origin/main -- <file>` proves current
   441	`main` has not changed that path since the PR base. For every overlapped
   442	source path, do a science-loss guard after integration: the current-main diff
   443	from `pr_base` to `origin/main` must still be represented in the final file.
   444	If that cannot be verified quickly, stop and treat it as a blocking integration
   445	hazard rather than risking science loss.
   446	
   447	Generated audit JSON/Markdown is a special case: do not hand-merge generated
   448	files from stale PR heads. Resolve source files first, prefer the current
   449	`origin/main` generated audit surface, then rerun the audit pipeline and strict
   450	lint to regenerate it.
   451	
   452	## Reviewer Fanout
   453	
   454	On each iteration, set `files_to_review` to the files that changed since their
   455	last clean review. On iteration 1, use all original changed files.
   456	
   457	Run every applicable reviewer lens. Under the shared-pool concurrency
   458	budget (Default Entry above), combine the lenses into one or two passes per
   459	PR — full per-lens parallel fanout through the available agent/subagent
   460	mechanism is the quiet-pool mode. If parallel agents are unavailable, run
   461	the same reviewer passes locally and report that limitation. In every mode,
   462	each applicable lens must be explicitly covered and named in the findings.
   463	
   464	### Required Reviewers
   465	
   466	- `CodeRunnerReviewer`
   467	  Review changed Python/scripts/log-producing code. Check syntax, decisive
   468	  assertions, hard-coded targets, stale fixtures, literal `True` checks,
   469	  hidden observations, reproducibility, paired runner/output agreement, and
   470	  whether the runner actually tests the note's load-bearing bridge. If a
   471	  runner checks audit-ledger dependency status, it must use the current
   472	  retained-grade set (`retained`, `retained_bounded`, `retained_no_go`) rather
   473	  than hard-coding stale expectations such as exactly `retained`.
   474	  For math-bearing runners, PASS output is not enough. Extract every
   475	  load-bearing formula, sign, factor, normalization, matrix identity,
   476	  optimizer objective, and expected numeric value from the changed code and
   477	  note, then verify them by an independent route before landing: manual
   478	  derivation against the note, symbolic simplification, small-case exhaustive
   479	  enumeration, a second implementation that does not share the same expression,
   480	  or invariant/limit/property checks. Treat self-confirming tests, expected
   481	  values generated by the same implementation under review, missing factor/sign
   482	  checks, or stale reopened bug reports as blocking until the formula is
   483	  corrected or the claim is demoted to a narrower supported boundary.
   484	
   485	- `PhysicsClaimReviewer`
   486	  Attack theorem notes, claims tables, publication surfaces, and prose. Check
   487	  semantic bridges, selector assumptions, status labels, exact/bounded/support
   488	  boundaries, and code/prose drift.
   489	
   490	- `ImportSupportReviewer`
   491	  Inventory every measured, fitted, literature, PDG, cosmological,
   492	  normalization, boundary-condition, or convention input. Classify each as
   493	  `zero-input structural`, `framework-derived`, `one computed lattice input`,
   494	  `explicit normalization/boundary condition`, `standard/literature
   495	  correction`, `observational comparator`, `support-only`, `insensitive
   496	  nuisance`, or `unjustified import`. For a Nature-grade retention claim, every
   497	  import must be derived, disclosed as a non-satisfying condition with a narrow role, quantitatively
   498	  insensitive, or the claim must be demoted.
   499	
   500	- `NatureRetentionReviewer`
   501	  Apply the hostile external-review bar. Ask whether the result can honestly
   502	  be called retained/Nature-grade: no hidden unit identification, no structural
   503	  redefinition, no imported selector, no unsupported first-principles claim,
   504	  no unmatched observed target, and clear falsifiers/open gates. Output
   505	  `RETAINED`, `RETAINED SUPPORT`, `BOUNDED`, `OPEN`, `NO-GO`, or `REJECT`.
   506	
   507	- `NoGoDisciplineReviewer`
   508	  Scrutinize negative claims with the same rigor as positive ones. Trigger
   509	  this reviewer whenever changed content includes a `no_go`, `stretch_attempt`,
   510	  `bounded_with_named_walls`, or derived-no-go-boundary artifact, or when any
   511	  other reviewer in this fanout outputs `NO-GO` / `BOUNDED` / `OVERCLAIM` on
   512	  a negative claim. The reviewer must invoke the `no-go-discipline` skill
   513	  and walk N1-N8 against the branch content (see
   514	  [`docs/ai_methodology/skills/no-go-discipline/SKILL.md`](../no-go-discipline/SKILL.md)):
   515	  N1 alternative-route enumeration (≥5 distinct routes), N2
   516	  wall-independence audit, N3 hidden-wall scan, N4 residual matching,
   517	  N5 rhetoric audit (per-element / per-mode / per-block / lattice-wide
   518	  resolutions), N6 partial-closure path scan (convention-reframe vs new
   519	  axiom), N7 steelman, N8 cross-cycle echo. Output `PASS` (negative claim
   520	  honestly scoped) or `FAIL` with the failing checklist items named and the
   521	  narrowest demoted claim proposed (`partial-attempt-with-named-untested-routes`,
   522	  `partial-narrowing`, `bounded-with-corrected-wall-count`, or
   523	  `stretch-attempt-with-honest-residual`). The reviewer must not approve a
   524	  no-go that has not been stress-tested against the framework's full
   525	  authority surface — under-tested negative claims are at least as harmful
   526	  as overclaimed positive ones because they foreclose investigation paths
   527	  permanently.
   528	
   529	- `LabelingConventionReviewer`
   530	  Detect labeling/naming/convention content masquerading as a bounded
   531	  theorem. Trigger whenever changed content includes a `bounded_theorem`
   532	  candidate whose load-bearing claim is a labeling/naming/convention
   533	  statement (parallel to the u/c/t mass-ordering convention or the
   534	  e/μ/τ charged-lepton naming) rather than an algebraic claim with
   535	  explicit named conditions. A labeling convention has no propositional
   536	  premise content, so `retained_bounded` grade does not apply — the
   537	  grade is for algebraic claims with explicit named premises, not for
   538	  stipulations about names.
   539	
   540	  The right outcome is to split:
   541	  (i) the algebraic core (if any) ships as a narrow `positive_theorem`
   542	      or `bounded_theorem` with the algebraic premises explicit;
   543	  (ii) the labeling content ships as a separate `meta` convention note,
   544	       parallel to the No-Go Discipline Battery's labeling-vs-physics
   545	       check in
   546	       `docs/ai_methodology/skills/physics-claim-reviewer/SKILL.md`
   547	       ("If labeling, the right outcome is a `meta` convention note").
   548	
   549	  Output `PASS` if the candidate is genuinely algebraic with named
   550	  conditions, `SPLIT-REQUIRED` if labeling content is bundled with
   551	  algebraic content (ship the algebraic theorem narrow + the convention
   552	  as a separate `meta` note), or `DEMOTE-TO-META` if the candidate is
   553	  purely convention with no derivation. The reviewer must not approve a
   554	  `bounded_theorem` whose load-bearing content is a labeling stipulation
   555	  — conflating conventions with bounded theorems hides which premises
   556	  are actually load-bearing and prevents downstream rows from cleanly
   557	  identifying their dependency status. Downstream costs of the
   558	  conflation: the bundled convention becomes an undischargeable
   559	  "premise" that blocks the row from reaching retained-unbounded;
   560	  downstream rows that cite the bundled bounded_theorem inherit an
   561	  unstated convention dependency; the audit lane cannot cleanly verify
   562	  "all premises retained" because the convention is not propositional
   563	  content; and future agents may waste cycles trying to "prove" the
   564	  convention as if it were derivable.
   565	
   566	- `RepoGovernanceReviewer`
   567	  Check placement and authority surfaces. Ensure live findings route through
   568	  `docs/repo/ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE.md`, long packets go under
   569	  `docs/work_history/repo/review_feedback/`, publication edits update the
   570	  relevant `docs/publication/ci3_z3/` surfaces, status wording follows
   571	  `docs/repo/CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY.md`, and changed claim notes are compatible
   572	  with the audit lane's propose/ratify split. Also verify that load-bearing
   573	  dependencies are real markdown links that seed the citation graph, not just
   574	  code-formatted file names in prose. Block ambiguous new science names such
   575	  as bare `A1`, `A2`, `G1`, `R3`, `Route F`, or `Block 2` when they appear as
   576	  titles, primary table labels, claim scopes, runner headlines, or review
   577	  findings without an explicit scientific noun phrase. Block repo-wide axiom
   578	  additions, nonstandard theory vocabulary, or new foundational claims unless
   579	  the user explicitly approved that change; vocabulary corrections back to
   580	  repo conventions are allowed.
   581	  Block branch-local or draft-PR language from landing on repo-facing surfaces.
   582	  Long-lived draft wording, PR-specific labels, campaign names, and branch-only
   583	  framings must be translated into native repo vocabulary before merge
   584	  (including language leaked from PR230 or any similar draft branch). If a
   585	  scientific claim is otherwise salvageable, fix the vocabulary in the landing
   586	  commit instead of rejecting the science.
   587	
   588	### Optional Reviewer
   589	
   590	Run `MethodologySkillReviewer` when files under `docs/ai_methodology/skills/`,
   591	`docs/ai_methodology/`, or `.claude/commands/` changed. Check that the skill is
   592	concise, triggerable from its frontmatter/command name, aligned with the AI
   593	methodology lane, and not claiming physics authority.
   594	
   595	## Reviewer Prompt
   596	
   597	Use this prompt shape for each reviewer, filtered to only that reviewer's file
   598	scope:
   599	
   600	````text
   601	Review the following physics-repo changes.
   602	
   603	Files to review:
   604	<files>
   605	
   606	Diff/content:
   607	```diff
   608	<diff for only those files; include untracked file content separately>
   609	```
   610	
   611	Focus:
   612	<focus text or "None specified">
   613	
   614	Context:
   615	- Base ref: <base-ref>
   616	- Iteration: <N> of <max>
   617	- Already reviewed and unchanged: <reviewed_files>
   618	- Repo review surfaces: REVIEW_FEEDBACK_WORKFLOW, ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE,
   619	  CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY, CANONICAL_HARNESS_INDEX, docs/audit/README.md
   620	
   621	Rules:
   622	- Findings must cite file/line when possible.
   623	- Separate bugs, overclaims, support-only demotions, imported-value problems,
   624	  repo-governance problems, and nits.
   625	- Do not require new science for wording problems.
   626	- Do not approve retained/Nature-grade language if an import or bridge remains
   627	  hidden.
   628	- Do not apply audit verdicts. Review only whether the branch is ready for the
   629	  independent audit worker.
   630	- Do not approve new bare letter-number science names. Require explicit names
   631	  from CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY, with shorthand only as a parenthetical alias.
   632	- Do not approve a `NO-GO` or `BOUNDED with named walls` recommendation
   633	  without running `no-go-discipline` N1-N8 against the branch content. An
   634	  unscrutinized negative claim forecloses investigation paths permanently and
   635	  is at least as harmful as an overclaimed positive.
   636	````
   637	
   638	## Consolidate Findings
   639	
   640	Present one iteration summary:
   641	
   642	```text
   643	## Review Results (Iteration N)
   644	
   645	### Code / Runner: PASS | RISK | FAIL
   646	### Physics Claim Boundary: RETAINED | SUPPORT | BOUNDED | OPEN | REJECT
   647	### Imports / Support: CLEAN | DISCLOSED | DEMOTE | FAIL
   648	### Nature Retention: RETAINED | RETAINED SUPPORT | BOUNDED | OPEN | NO-GO | REJECT
   649	### No-Go Discipline: PASS | FAIL | NOT APPLICABLE
   650	### Labeling Convention: PASS | SPLIT-REQUIRED | DEMOTE-TO-META | NOT APPLICABLE
   651	### Repo Governance: PASS | FIX | QUEUE | ARCHIVE
   652	### Audit Compatibility: PASS | FIX | BLOCKED | NOT APPLICABLE
   653	### Methodology Skill: PASS | FIX | SKIPPED
   654	```
   655	
   656	Classify every finding:
   657	
   658	- `BUG`
   659	- `OVERCLAIM`
   660	- `NO_GO_OVERCLAIM`
   661	- `IMPORTED_VALUE`
   662	- `SUPPORT_ONLY_DEMOTION`
   663	- `MISSING_ARTIFACT`
   664	- `SEMANTIC_BRIDGE`
   665	- `REPO_GOVERNANCE`
   666	- `AUDIT_COMPATIBILITY`
   667	- `NIT`
   668	- `SALVAGE_CANDIDATE`
   669	- `SALVAGE_REJECT`
   670	
   671	Stop immediately when all applicable reviewers are clean.
   672	
   673	## Salvage Pass
   674	
   675	Run this pass before closing a PR, marking it non-landable, or discarding a
   676	stretch/campaign packet. The goal is to preserve meaningful science without
   677	lowering the review bar.
   678	
   679	1. Inventory the branch into these buckets:
   680	   - canonical source candidates: theorem/no-go/open-gate notes and paired
   681	     runners;
   682	   - useful negative results: failed routes that name a durable obstruction and
   683	     have a runner or exact calculation;
   684	   - support-only calculations: exact algebra or bookkeeping that may be useful
   685	     as bounded support but not as retained/Nature-grade science;
   686	   - audit/process hygiene: dependency-graph repairs, audit queue unlocks,
   687	     stale runner-cache detection, generated-data normalization, cycle-break
   688	     hygiene, and pipeline/tooling fixes that make audit results more reliable;
   689	   - non-source material: claim-status certificates, handoffs, campaign state,
   690	     generated audit files, expected audit verdicts, and branch-local logs.
   691	2. For each source candidate, decide whether it can be salvaged with only
   692	   review-level edits:
   693	   - the claim can be narrowed to a canonical `claim_type`:
   694	     `positive_theorem`, `bounded_theorem`, `no_go`, `open_gate`,
   695	     `decoration`, or `meta`;
   696	   - all imported physics, textbook machinery, observations, fitted values,
   697	     and conventions are explicitly labelled;
   698	   - the runner tests the actual load-bearing bridge, not just downstream
   699	     arithmetic after the premise is assumed;
   700	   - load-bearing dependencies can be represented as markdown links and
   701	     non-load-bearing siblings can be kept out of the citation graph;
   702	   - the salvage does not rely on a closed, unlanded, unaudited, or rejected
   703	     sibling PR unless the dependency is copied in as a self-contained
   704	     derivation and reviewed in the same salvage branch.
   705	3. Do not salvage by papering over missing science. If the durable part is
   706	   only an obstruction or failed route, salvage it as a narrow `open_gate` or
   707	   `no_go` only when the runner directly supports that negative boundary.
   708	4. Strip all non-source material from salvage branches:
   709	   claim-status certificates, handoffs, campaign state, expected audit
   710	   verdicts, `target_effective_status_*`, `audit_status = ...`, generated audit
   711	   verdict payloads, and branch-local logs.
   712	5. Prefer small salvage slices grouped by coherent topic. Split unrelated
   713	   lemmas rather than bundling them only because they came from the same failed
   714	   PR, but do not open follow-up PRs for those slices. Land them through the
   715	   current requested landing path or report that the work cannot be landed yet.
   716	6. Run the normal audit-system compatibility gate on every salvage slice.
   717	   The resulting rows must remain `unaudited`; the independent audit lane owns
   718	   all verdicts.
   719	7. For audit/process hygiene, preserve the durable repair rather than the
   720	   generated symptom. Land source/tooling/pipeline/controlled-data changes when
   721	   they strengthen the repo or unblock auditing without changing science.
   722	   Regenerate audit JSON/Markdown from the pipeline afterward only from the
   723	   reviewed source repair on current `main`. Do not land PR-authored
   724	   `effective_status`, `intrinsic_status`, `audit_status`, auditor-output,
   725	   previous-audit, or expected-verdict edits as the authority for the change.
   726	   Source repairs may intentionally invalidate a prior row hash and make a row
   727	   visible for re-audit; that is allowed. The independent audit loop must still
   728	   produce the verdict after landing.
   729	8. If no salvage is possible, leave a concise PR comment or review summary
   730	   saying why, for example: "runner only rechecks assumed premise",
   731	   "claim depends on closed sibling", "noncanonical stretch packet with no
   732	   theorem-grade boundary", or "overbroad theorem not supported by runner".
   733	
   734	Salvageable examples:
   735	
   736	- a parity/counting/no-go lemma with a decisive finite algebra runner;
   737	- a conditional textbook lemma that is useful only when explicitly marked as
   738	  bounded support;
   739	- a negative route that conclusively rules out one proposed mechanism and
   740	  narrows the remaining open gate;
   741	- an audit-hygiene PR whose generated status change reveals a real durable
   742	  graph/tooling/pipeline defect, salvaged as the underlying repair plus
   743	  regenerated audit outputs.
   744	
   745	Not salvageable without a new research task:
   746	
   747	- branch-local certificates and handoffs with no source theorem;
   748	- broad "closing derivations" whose runner assumes the missing bridge;
   749	- expected audit verdicts or status-elevation packages;
   750	- stretch-attempt notes that document research direction but do not define a
   751	  canonical theorem/no-go/open-gate boundary.
   752	
   753	## Fix Policy
   754	
   755	If `--no-fix` was passed, do not edit.
   756	
   757	Otherwise apply the narrowest honest fix:
   758	
   759	1. Fix verified code bugs, broken reproduction commands, stale runner names,
   760	   false PASS checks, and code/prose mismatches.
   761	2. Demote overclaimed status when the artifact supports only support/bounded
   762	   language.
   763	3. Mark imported values explicitly; distinguish derived, conditional, fitted,
   764	   measured, literature, boundary-condition, and insensitive nuisance inputs.
   765	4. Add or repair paired runner/note references only when the artifact exists.
   766	5. Make audit-system hygiene fixes only when they do not change the science:
   767	   status-line tier labels, machine-local path removal, stale runner transcript
   768	   refreshes, generated audit queue/ledger seeding, and discoverability wiring.
   769	6. Rename ambiguous science shorthand to explicit repo vocabulary without
   770	   changing the claim boundary. Examples: write `one-qubit operator algebra`
   771	   (or equivalently `M_2(ℂ) ≅ Cl(3,0)`, `physical Cl(3) local algebra` as
   772	   the real-algebra reading — all co-equal labels for the same retained
   773	   algebra-isomorphism class), `Z^3 lattice`,
   774	   `Koide Frobenius-equipartition condition`, or `Lie type A_1` instead of
   775	   bare `A1` / `A2`.
   776	7. Update `docs/repo/ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE.md` for live unresolved findings.
   777	8. Route detailed resolved packets to
   778	   `docs/work_history/repo/review_feedback/` only when a long packet is needed.
   779	9. When a PR is non-landable but salvageable, preserve only the durable
   780	   note/runner content, make the claim boundary canonical, and land that source
   781	   salvage through the current requested landing path. If the rejected branch
   782	   contains substantial non-source packet material, use a clean temporary
   783	   worktree for integration, but do not create or open a follow-up PR.
   784	
   785	Skip:
   786	
   787	- nits;
   788	- suspected findings without evidence;
   789	- ambiguous science gaps that need new derivation;
   790	- attempts to paper over missing theorem steps with confident prose;
   791	- repo-wide axiom additions, new theory terminology, or new foundational
   792	  premises that lack explicit user approval;
   793	- broad refactors unrelated to the finding.
   794	
   795	## Audit-System Compatibility Gate
   796	
   797	This gate is mandatory when a branch adds or edits source notes, runners,
   798	claim tables, lane stubs, or publication/control-plane files.
   799	
   800	The review loop must enforce the audit lane's propose/ratify split without
   801	performing the independent audit:
   802	
   803	**Audit-hash churn guard.** Non-semantic hygiene sweeps on audited source notes
   804	can be scientifically harmless while still invalidating large parts of the
   805	audit ledger, because note hashes are source-content hashes. Before landing any
   806	branch that touches many existing claim-note files for formatting, link-target,
   807	path, vocabulary, or other non-science cleanup, run the pipeline in validation
   808	mode and inspect the `seed_audit_ledger.py` / `invalidate_stale_audits.py`
   809	counts. If the change would reset or requeue already-audited rows solely due to
   810	non-semantic churn, do not land the broad source sweep. Either narrow the PR to
   811	non-ledger/non-claim surfaces, land a reviewed hash/canonicalization tooling
   812	repair first, or ask for explicit user approval to spend the audit capacity.
   813	Never trade a clean audit graph for cosmetic source-note churn without making
   814	that cost explicit.
   815	
   816	0. Before applying a PR, inventory any audit-status surface it touches:
   817	
   818	```bash
   819	git diff --name-only <pr-base>..refs/tmp/pr-<N> -- \
   820	  docs/audit/AUDIT_LEDGER.md docs/audit/AUDIT_QUEUE.md docs/audit/data \
   821	  'docs/publication/ci3_z3/*_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md'
   822	git diff <pr-base>..refs/tmp/pr-<N> -- docs/audit docs/publication/ci3_z3 \
   823	  | grep -E 'audit_status|effective_status|audited_clean|audited_conditional|audited_failed|audited_renaming|audited_decoration|audited_numerical_match|previous_audits|audit_result|verdict'
   824	```
   825	
   826	Treat this output as a provenance review, not as a merge recipe. Strip
   827	PR-submitted generated ledgers, queues, effective-status tables, auditor
   828	transcripts, and audit verdict payloads before landing. The only acceptable
   829	audit-lane changes from a PR are reviewed source/tooling repairs and
   830	machine-readable audit/re-audit targeting metadata, such as dispatcher
   831	sidecars, that do not assert a verdict. After applying the source repair, run
   832	the local pipeline to verify the row is queued or re-queued as intended, then
   833	restore generated audit outputs from `origin/main` before committing. Pipeline
   834	regeneration of `docs/audit/data/`, `docs/audit/AUDIT_LEDGER.md`,
   835	`docs/audit/AUDIT_QUEUE.md`, `docs/audit/MISSING_DERIVATION_PROMPTS.md`, and
   836	`docs/publication/ci3_z3/*_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md` is a VALIDATION step only;
   837	framework PRs must never ship these files because the merge would overwrite
   838	the audit lane's ratified state. The audit-loop run on `main` (nightly cron
   839	plus `audit:` commits) is the sole channel for landing those outputs.
   840	
   841	1. Source-note `Status:` prose is not an audit authority. New or touched claim
   842	   notes should use `Type:` / `Claim type:` metadata for intended audit
   843	   classification.
   844	2. If a no-go/firewall is intended to be theorem-grade, use
   845	   `claim_type = no_go`; do not rely on support-style prose and expect audit
   846	   ratification.
   847	3. Keep disclaimers such as "This is not charged-lepton mass closure" outside
   848	   audit metadata fields.
   849	4. Do not prefill or recommend a verdict in author/review surfaces. Wording
   850	   such as `target_audit_status: audited_clean`, `audit_status =
   851	   audited_clean`, `effective_status = retained`, or "can land audited_clean"
   852	   is not review-loop compatible. Use wording like `audit_status_authority:
   853	   independent audit lane only` and "effective status is pipeline-derived
   854	   after audit ratification and dependency closure."
   855	5. Changed claim notes that cite load-bearing authorities must use markdown
   856	   links, for example
   857	   ``[`GRAPH_FIRST_SU3_INTEGRATION_NOTE.md`](GRAPH_FIRST_SU3_INTEGRATION_NOTE.md)``.
   858	   Code-formatted names such as `` `GRAPH_FIRST_SU3_INTEGRATION_NOTE.md` `` do
   859	   not seed graph dependencies and are not enough.
   860	6. Run the audit pipeline after review fixes:
   861	
   862	```bash
   863	bash docs/audit/scripts/run_pipeline.sh
   864	python3 docs/audit/scripts/audit_lint.py --strict
   865	git diff --check
   866	```
   867	
   868	The known graph-cycle warning is acceptable. Any strict-lint error blocks a
   869	review-loop PASS.
   870	
   871	**`note_hash` drift is a notice for non-retained rows, an error only for
   872	retained-grade rows.** `note_hash` is a *source-content* hash, not an audit
   873	verdict. When a review fix edits a claim note, its `note_hash` drifts from the
   874	seeded value; `audit_lint.py` reports this drift as a non-blocking
   875	`note_hash_drift_reaudit_pending` **notice** when the row is not retained-grade
   876	(`unaudited` / `audited_conditional` / pending), because re-audit is simply
   877	pending and the audit-lane re-seed refreshes the hash. Such a notice does **not**
   878	block review-loop PASS and must **not** be "fixed" by committing audit-lane
   879	ledger churn (that is the forbidden pipeline-output commit). A `note_hash`
   880	mismatch on a **retained-grade** row (`retained` / `retained_bounded` /
   881	`retained_no_go`) stays a hard **error**: an edited retained note laundered past
   882	a stale ratification is a real integrity violation. Resolve it by re-auditing
   883	(the audit lane re-seeds and archives the prior verdict) or by demoting the edit
   884	per the audit-hash churn guard — never by refreshing the hash while keeping the
   885	retained verdict.
   886	
   887	**Stuck-row repair requeue gate.** Terminal non-clean rows
   888	(`audited_conditional` / `audited_renaming` / `audited_failed` /
   889	`audited_numerical_match`) re-enter the audit queue only through their own
   890	note or paired-runner hash drift, an upstream `deps_changed` invalidation, or
   891	a dispatcher-sidecar re-audit target. Dependent-side edits never reschedule
   892	the stuck row. When a branch's stated purpose is repairing such a row (the PR
   893	title/body names the row or quotes its audit repair target):
   894	
   895	1. Verify the stuck row itself will requeue: its note or paired runner
   896	   changes on the branch, or the branch ships dispatcher-sidecar targeting
   897	   metadata naming the row.
   898	2. If the audit-named repair is dependent-side only (for example, narrowing
   899	   dependents' citing sentences to the audited scope), add a dated
   900	   downstream-hygiene line to the stuck row's own note boundary as part of
   901	   the landing: a one-line source-side record of what changed downstream
   902	   (date + what was narrowed + PR number), with no grade or verdict
   903	   language. The hash drift re-enters the row into the ordinary queue and
   904	   the re-auditor (or second auditor) sees the recorded condition.
   905	3. Run the validation pipeline and confirm the row is queued or re-queued as
   906	   intended, then restore generated audit outputs per the
   907	   pipeline-output-stripped gate below.
   908	4. Repair-PR review checklist: the audit repair target is quoted verbatim
   909	   (from `verdict_rationale` / `notes_for_re_audit_if_any`) in the PR body;
   910	   a sibling-runner pin sweep was done before every note edit (grep
   911	   `scripts/` for runners pinning the edited sentences); no authored grade
   912	   language anywhere; no `docs/audit/data/` content beyond
   913	   dispatcher-sidecar targeting metadata.
   914	
   915	7. **Pipeline-output-stripped PASS gate (hard).** After running the pipeline
   916	   for validation, the framework PR must NOT land any pipeline-regenerated
   917	   audit-lane or effective-status surface. The independent audit lane is the
   918	   sole authority for these files; a framework PR that ships them creates a
   919	   dual-source-of-truth and overwrites the audit lane's ratified state at
   920	   merge. The following must hold for review-loop to issue PASS:
   921	
   922	```bash
   923	# Must produce no output. Any change here means the working tree has
   924	# pipeline-regenerated audit-lane outputs left over from validation;
   925	# drop them (see below) before recommitting.
   926	git status --porcelain docs/audit/AUDIT_LEDGER.md \
   927	                       docs/audit/AUDIT_QUEUE.md \
   928	                       docs/audit/data \
   929	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/PUBLICATION_AUDIT_DIVERGENCE.md \
   930	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/CLAIMS_TABLE_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
   931	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/DERIVATION_ATLAS_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
   932	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/PUBLICATION_MATRIX_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
   933	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/FULL_CLAIM_LEDGER_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
   934	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/USABLE_DERIVED_VALUES_INDEX_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
   935	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/RESULTS_INDEX_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
   936	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/QUANTITATIVE_SUMMARY_TABLE_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
   937	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/DERIVATION_VALIDATION_MAP_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md
   938	```
   939	
   940	If this command prints any lines, BLOCK PASS and instruct the operator to
   941	DROP the regenerated files before recommitting:
   942	
   943	```bash
   944	git checkout origin/main -- docs/audit/data/ \
   945	                            docs/audit/AUDIT_QUEUE.md \
   946	                            docs/audit/MISSING_DERIVATION_PROMPTS.md \
   947	                            'docs/publication/ci3_z3/*_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md' \
   948	                            docs/publication/ci3_z3/PUBLICATION_AUDIT_DIVERGENCE.md
   949	git clean -fd -- docs/audit/data/
   950	```
   951	
   952	The pipeline is run for VALIDATION only — to confirm the source repair is
   953	ingested and the runner row is queued or re-queued as intended. The
   954	audit-loop pipeline run on `main` (nightly cron + `audit:` commits) is the
   955	sole channel for landing the regenerated outputs. Framework PRs that ship
   956	these files force a destructive overwrite of ratified audit state at merge
   957	time and have been an active source of broken-row regressions.
   958	
   959	8. **Repository-portable links PASS gate (hard).** Markdown link targets on
   960	   branch-modified `.md` files must be repo-relative or web URLs. Absolute
   961	   local paths such as `/Users/<name>/...`, `/home/<name>/...`,
   962	   `/private/tmp/...`, `/tmp/...`, `/var/...`, `/opt/...`, or `file://...`
   963	   inside a markdown link target are non-portable: they break for other
   964	   developers, CI runners, fresh clones, and independent reviewers.
   965	
   966	```bash
   967	# Must produce no output. Scans branch-modified markdown for local absolute
   968	# paths inside markdown link targets.
   969	git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- '*.md' \
   970	  | xargs -I{} grep -nE '\]\((/Users/|/home/|/private/|/tmp/|/var/|/opt/|file://)' {} 2>/dev/null
   971	```
   972	
   973	If this command prints lines for files the branch is already modifying for
   974	source, runner, methodology, or review reasons, rewrite the offending link
   975	targets before PASS. The usual mechanical fix is to preserve the display text
   976	and replace the target with a `../` chain relative to the source file's
   977	directory, e.g. in `docs/SOURCE_RESOLVED_FOO_NOTE.md` rewrite
   978	`(/Users/me/Projects/Physics/scripts/foo.py)` to `(../scripts/foo.py)`.
   979	
   980	This gate prevents new non-portable links from landing; it is not a license for
   981	large standalone cosmetic sweeps over audited claim notes. If the PR's only
   982	purpose is to rewrite existing local-path links across many audited source
   983	notes, apply the audit-hash churn guard above before landing any broad cleanup.
   984	
   985	9. **No-Go Discipline PASS gate (hard).** Before issuing review-loop PASS,
   986	   identify any artifact on the branch that ships a negative claim:
   987	
   988	```bash
   989	# Source notes whose claim_type is no_go, or whose Status / Type line
   990	# names walls / open conditions / "conditional on" content
   991	git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- 'docs/*NO_GO*.md' 'docs/*BOUNDED*.md' \
   992	                                           'docs/*STRETCH_ATTEMPT*.md' \
   993	                                           'docs/*OBSTRUCTION*.md'
   994	# Audit-data shards whose verdict_rationale or claim_type record walls
   995	git diff origin/main...HEAD -- docs/audit/data/ledger docs/audit/data/ledger_meta.json \
   996	  | grep -E '"claim_type": "no_go"|"verdict_rationale".*wall|"verdict_rationale".*condition'
   997	# Any source note touched on this branch whose body contains negative-claim shape
   998	git diff origin/main...HEAD -- 'docs/*.md' \
   999	  | grep -E 'structurally undecidable|no retained primitive|requires new axiom|cannot be derived from A_min|conditional on .* walls?'
  1000	```
  1001	
  1002	For every match, the NoGoDisciplineReviewer must output `PASS` (N1-N8 walk
  1003	complete and no failure condition hit) before review-loop issues PASS. A
  1004	`FAIL` from NoGoDisciplineReviewer blocks PASS regardless of how other
  1005	reviewers voted. An unscrutinized no-go that ships through review cements
  1006	the overclaim at audit time and forecloses investigation paths permanently.
  1007	
  1008	If NoGoDisciplineReviewer outputs FAIL, apply the narrowest honest fix per
  1009	Fix Policy step 2 (demote to a narrower honest claim that passes N1-N8) and
  1010	re-review. Do not weaken the gate to PASS the branch.
  1011	
  1012	This gate is independent of the Pipeline-clean PASS gate above; both must
  1013	pass for review-loop to issue PASS.
  1014	
  1015	10. **Math-runner independent-check PASS gate (hard).** Before issuing
  1016	review-loop PASS for any branch that changes a runner, proof script, numeric
  1017	constant, matrix construction, optimizer, expected value, or note formula,
  1018	record the independent math check used by `CodeRunnerReviewer`. At least one
  1019	check must not share the same implementation path as the changed runner:
  1020	manual formula derivation, symbolic/algebraic reduction, finite toy-case
  1021	enumeration, independent recomputation, or invariant/limit tests. A runner
  1022	that merely computes its own target and prints PASS is not a proof that the
  1023	formula is correct. If an issue was reopened because the runner's math was
  1024	wrong, treat the whole formula family as suspect until the changed expression
  1025	and any reused helpers are cross-checked.
  1026	
  1027	11. **Native-language PASS gate (hard).** Changed repo-facing text must use
  1028	controlled, native repo vocabulary. Run `scripts/vocab_lint.py --fix` on all
  1029	branch-modified files before landing, then inspect changed headings, metadata,
  1030	runner banners, claim scopes, table labels, and review comments for
  1031	branch-local/draft language that the linter cannot know about. PR-specific
  1032	labels, draft-branch vocabulary, campaign names, and noncanonical theory
  1033	phrases must be rewritten into repo-native language or explicitly deferred in
  1034	`docs/repo/ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE.md`; do not land them silently.
  1035	
  1036	The review loop must not run `docs/audit/scripts/apply_audit.py` and must not
  1037	write `audit_status`, `audited_clean`, or other audit verdicts. If the branch
  1038	introduces retained-grade `claim_type` rows, report those claim IDs in the
  1039	final report as requiring the independent audit worker.
  1040	When a source repair changes a note or runner for a previously audited row,
  1041	the local result is `note_hash`/runner-hash drift plus queue/dispatch
  1042	visibility for independent re-audit. For a non-retained row this drift is a
  1043	benign `note_hash_drift_reaudit_pending` notice (see the Audit-System
  1044	Compatibility Gate) — it does not block strict lint and must not be repaired by
  1045	committing ledger churn. For a retained-grade row the drift is a strict error
  1046	that must be resolved by re-audit, not laundered. In all cases, do not preserve,
  1047	copy, or author a fresh `previous_audits` entry, `audit_status`, or verdict
  1048	rationale from the PR branch; the independent audit lane (nightly cron +
  1049	`audit:` commits) is the sole channel that refreshes the hash and re-ratifies.
  1050	
  1051	After the pipeline, inspect the changed claim rows in
  1052	`docs/audit/data/audit_ledger.json`:
  1053	
  1054	- `claim_type` must match the intended class (`positive_theorem`,
  1055	  `bounded_theorem`, `no_go`, `open_gate`, `decoration`, or `meta`).
  1056	- `audit_status` must remain `unaudited` unless the branch is only carrying
  1057	  already-audited history from `origin/main`.
  1058	- `effective_status` must be pipeline-derived, not hand-authored.
  1059	- New theorem/no-go/bounded rows with declared load-bearing authorities must
  1060	  have non-empty `deps` matching the markdown-linked authorities.
  1061	- Dependencies asserted as retained-grade must currently have
  1062	  `effective_status` in `{retained, retained_bounded, retained_no_go}`. Open
  1063	  gates, `unaudited`, `audit_in_progress`, `retained_pending_chain`, and
  1064	  terminal non-clean audit statuses are blockers for retained-grade claims.
  1065	
  1066	Useful review-only inventory:
  1067	
  1068	```bash
  1069	python3 - <<'PY'
  1070	import json, subprocess
  1071	changed = set()
  1072	for cmd in (
  1073	    ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "HEAD"],
  1074	    ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--cached"],
  1075	):
  1076	    changed.update(subprocess.check_output(cmd, text=True).splitlines())
  1077	try:
  1078	    changed.update(subprocess.check_output(
  1079	        ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "origin/main...HEAD"], text=True
  1080	    ).splitlines())
  1081	except Exception:
  1082	
  1083	exec
  1084	/bin/zsh -lc "wc -l /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md && sed -n '500,650p' /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md && sed -n '651,800p' /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md && sed -n '801,950p' /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md && sed -n '951,1100p' /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md" in /Users/jonBridger/Toy Physics/.claude/worktrees/quirky-wiles-92e3b4
  1085	 succeeded in 0ms:
  1086	    1111 /Users/jonBridger/.codex/skills/review-loop/SKILL.md
  1087	  (i) the algebraic core (if any) ships as a narrow `positive_theorem`
  1088	      or `bounded_theorem` with the algebraic premises explicit;
  1089	  (ii) the labeling content ships as a separate `meta` convention note,
  1090	       parallel to the No-Go Discipline Battery's labeling-vs-physics
  1091	       check in
  1092	       `docs/ai_methodology/skills/physics-claim-reviewer/SKILL.md`
  1093	       ("If labeling, the right outcome is a `meta` convention note").
  1094	
  1095	  Output `PASS` if the candidate is genuinely algebraic with named
  1096	  conditions, `SPLIT-REQUIRED` if labeling content is bundled with
  1097	  algebraic content (ship the algebraic theorem narrow + the convention
  1098	  as a separate `meta` note), or `DEMOTE-TO-META` if the candidate is
  1099	  purely convention with no derivation. The reviewer must not approve a
  1100	  `bounded_theorem` whose load-bearing content is a labeling stipulation
  1101	  — conflating conventions with bounded theorems hides which premises
  1102	  are actually load-bearing and prevents downstream rows from cleanly
  1103	  identifying their dependency status. Downstream costs of the
  1104	  conflation: the bundled convention becomes an undischargeable
  1105	  "premise" that blocks the row from reaching retained-unbounded;
  1106	  downstream rows that cite the bundled bounded_theorem inherit an
  1107	  unstated convention dependency; the audit lane cannot cleanly verify
  1108	  "all premises retained" because the convention is not propositional
  1109	  content; and future agents may waste cycles trying to "prove" the
  1110	  convention as if it were derivable.
  1111	
  1112	- `RepoGovernanceReviewer`
  1113	  Check placement and authority surfaces. Ensure live findings route through
  1114	  `docs/repo/ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE.md`, long packets go under
  1115	  `docs/work_history/repo/review_feedback/`, publication edits update the
  1116	  relevant `docs/publication/ci3_z3/` surfaces, status wording follows
  1117	  `docs/repo/CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY.md`, and changed claim notes are compatible
  1118	  with the audit lane's propose/ratify split. Also verify that load-bearing
  1119	  dependencies are real markdown links that seed the citation graph, not just
  1120	  code-formatted file names in prose. Block ambiguous new science names such
  1121	  as bare `A1`, `A2`, `G1`, `R3`, `Route F`, or `Block 2` when they appear as
  1122	  titles, primary table labels, claim scopes, runner headlines, or review
  1123	  findings without an explicit scientific noun phrase. Block repo-wide axiom
  1124	  additions, nonstandard theory vocabulary, or new foundational claims unless
  1125	  the user explicitly approved that change; vocabulary corrections back to
  1126	  repo conventions are allowed.
  1127	  Block branch-local or draft-PR language from landing on repo-facing surfaces.
  1128	  Long-lived draft wording, PR-specific labels, campaign names, and branch-only
  1129	  framings must be translated into native repo vocabulary before merge
  1130	  (including language leaked from PR230 or any similar draft branch). If a
  1131	  scientific claim is otherwise salvageable, fix the vocabulary in the landing
  1132	  commit instead of rejecting the science.

  1134	### Optional Reviewer
  1135	
  1136	Run `MethodologySkillReviewer` when files under `docs/ai_methodology/skills/`,
  1137	`docs/ai_methodology/`, or `.claude/commands/` changed. Check that the skill is
  1138	concise, triggerable from its frontmatter/command name, aligned with the AI
  1139	methodology lane, and not claiming physics authority.
