  1141	## Reviewer Prompt
  1142	
  1143	Use this prompt shape for each reviewer, filtered to only that reviewer's file
  1144	scope:
  1145	
  1146	````text
  1147	Review the following physics-repo changes.
  1148	
  1149	Files to review:
  1150	<files>
  1151	
  1152	Diff/content:
  1153	```diff
  1154	<diff for only those files; include untracked file content separately>
  1155	```
  1156	
  1157	Focus:
  1158	<focus text or "None specified">
  1159	
  1160	Context:
  1161	- Base ref: <base-ref>
  1162	- Iteration: <N> of <max>
  1163	- Already reviewed and unchanged: <reviewed_files>
  1164	- Repo review surfaces: REVIEW_FEEDBACK_WORKFLOW, ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE,
  1165	  CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY, CANONICAL_HARNESS_INDEX, docs/audit/README.md
  1166	
  1167	Rules:
  1168	- Findings must cite file/line when possible.
  1169	- Separate bugs, overclaims, support-only demotions, imported-value problems,
  1170	  repo-governance problems, and nits.
  1171	- Do not require new science for wording problems.
  1172	- Do not approve retained/Nature-grade language if an import or bridge remains
  1173	  hidden.
  1174	- Do not apply audit verdicts. Review only whether the branch is ready for the
  1175	  independent audit worker.
  1176	- Do not approve new bare letter-number science names. Require explicit names
  1177	  from CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY, with shorthand only as a parenthetical alias.
  1178	- Do not approve a `NO-GO` or `BOUNDED with named walls` recommendation
  1179	  without running `no-go-discipline` N1-N8 against the branch content. An
  1180	  unscrutinized negative claim forecloses investigation paths permanently and
  1181	  is at least as harmful as an overclaimed positive.
  1182	````
  1183	
  1184	## Consolidate Findings
  1185	
  1186	Present one iteration summary:
  1187	
  1188	```text
  1189	## Review Results (Iteration N)
  1190	
  1191	### Code / Runner: PASS | RISK | FAIL
  1192	### Physics Claim Boundary: RETAINED | SUPPORT | BOUNDED | OPEN | REJECT
  1193	### Imports / Support: CLEAN | DISCLOSED | DEMOTE | FAIL
  1194	### Nature Retention: RETAINED | RETAINED SUPPORT | BOUNDED | OPEN | NO-GO | REJECT
  1195	### No-Go Discipline: PASS | FAIL | NOT APPLICABLE
  1196	### Labeling Convention: PASS | SPLIT-REQUIRED | DEMOTE-TO-META | NOT APPLICABLE
  1197	### Repo Governance: PASS | FIX | QUEUE | ARCHIVE
  1198	### Audit Compatibility: PASS | FIX | BLOCKED | NOT APPLICABLE
  1199	### Methodology Skill: PASS | FIX | SKIPPED
  1200	```
  1201	
  1202	Classify every finding:
  1203	
  1204	- `BUG`
  1205	- `OVERCLAIM`
  1206	- `NO_GO_OVERCLAIM`
  1207	- `IMPORTED_VALUE`
  1208	- `SUPPORT_ONLY_DEMOTION`
  1209	- `MISSING_ARTIFACT`
  1210	- `SEMANTIC_BRIDGE`
  1211	- `REPO_GOVERNANCE`
  1212	- `AUDIT_COMPATIBILITY`
  1213	- `NIT`
  1214	- `SALVAGE_CANDIDATE`
  1215	- `SALVAGE_REJECT`
  1216	
  1217	Stop immediately when all applicable reviewers are clean.
  1218	
  1219	## Salvage Pass
  1220	
  1221	Run this pass before closing a PR, marking it non-landable, or discarding a
  1222	stretch/campaign packet. The goal is to preserve meaningful science without
  1223	lowering the review bar.
  1224	
  1225	1. Inventory the branch into these buckets:
  1226	   - canonical source candidates: theorem/no-go/open-gate notes and paired
  1227	     runners;
  1228	   - useful negative results: failed routes that name a durable obstruction and
  1229	     have a runner or exact calculation;
  1230	   - support-only calculations: exact algebra or bookkeeping that may be useful
  1231	     as bounded support but not as retained/Nature-grade science;
  1232	   - audit/process hygiene: dependency-graph repairs, audit queue unlocks,
  1233	     stale runner-cache detection, generated-data normalization, cycle-break
  1234	     hygiene, and pipeline/tooling fixes that make audit results more reliable;
  1235	   - non-source material: claim-status certificates, handoffs, campaign state,
  1236	     generated audit files, expected audit verdicts, and branch-local logs.
  1237	2. For each source candidate, decide whether it can be salvaged with only
  1238	   review-level edits:
  1239	   - the claim can be narrowed to a canonical `claim_type`:
  1240	     `positive_theorem`, `bounded_theorem`, `no_go`, `open_gate`,
  1241	     `decoration`, or `meta`;
  1242	   - all imported physics, textbook machinery, observations, fitted values,
  1243	     and conventions are explicitly labelled;
  1244	   - the runner tests the actual load-bearing bridge, not just downstream
  1245	     arithmetic after the premise is assumed;
  1246	   - load-bearing dependencies can be represented as markdown links and
  1247	     non-load-bearing siblings can be kept out of the citation graph;
  1248	   - the salvage does not rely on a closed, unlanded, unaudited, or rejected
  1249	     sibling PR unless the dependency is copied in as a self-contained
  1250	     derivation and reviewed in the same salvage branch.
  1251	3. Do not salvage by papering over missing science. If the durable part is
  1252	   only an obstruction or failed route, salvage it as a narrow `open_gate` or
  1253	   `no_go` only when the runner directly supports that negative boundary.
  1254	4. Strip all non-source material from salvage branches:
  1255	   claim-status certificates, handoffs, campaign state, expected audit
  1256	   verdicts, `target_effective_status_*`, `audit_status = ...`, generated audit
  1257	   verdict payloads, and branch-local logs.
  1258	5. Prefer small salvage slices grouped by coherent topic. Split unrelated
  1259	   lemmas rather than bundling them only because they came from the same failed
  1260	   PR, but do not open follow-up PRs for those slices. Land them through the
  1261	   current requested landing path or report that the work cannot be landed yet.
  1262	6. Run the normal audit-system compatibility gate on every salvage slice.
  1263	   The resulting rows must remain `unaudited`; the independent audit lane owns
  1264	   all verdicts.
  1265	7. For audit/process hygiene, preserve the durable repair rather than the
  1266	   generated symptom. Land source/tooling/pipeline/controlled-data changes when
  1267	   they strengthen the repo or unblock auditing without changing science.
  1268	   Regenerate audit JSON/Markdown from the pipeline afterward only from the
  1269	   reviewed source repair on current `main`. Do not land PR-authored
  1270	   `effective_status`, `intrinsic_status`, `audit_status`, auditor-output,
  1271	   previous-audit, or expected-verdict edits as the authority for the change.
  1272	   Source repairs may intentionally invalidate a prior row hash and make a row
  1273	   visible for re-audit; that is allowed. The independent audit loop must still
  1274	   produce the verdict after landing.
  1275	8. If no salvage is possible, leave a concise PR comment or review summary
  1276	   saying why, for example: "runner only rechecks assumed premise",
  1277	   "claim depends on closed sibling", "noncanonical stretch packet with no
  1278	   theorem-grade boundary", or "overbroad theorem not supported by runner".
  1279	
  1280	Salvageable examples:
  1281	
  1282	- a parity/counting/no-go lemma with a decisive finite algebra runner;
  1283	- a conditional textbook lemma that is useful only when explicitly marked as
  1284	  bounded support;
  1285	- a negative route that conclusively rules out one proposed mechanism and
  1286	  narrows the remaining open gate;
  1287	- an audit-hygiene PR whose generated status change reveals a real durable
  1288	  graph/tooling/pipeline defect, salvaged as the underlying repair plus
  1289	  regenerated audit outputs.
  1290	
  1291	Not salvageable without a new research task:
  1292	
  1293	- branch-local certificates and handoffs with no source theorem;
  1294	- broad "closing derivations" whose runner assumes the missing bridge;
  1295	- expected audit verdicts or status-elevation packages;
  1296	- stretch-attempt notes that document research direction but do not define a
  1297	  canonical theorem/no-go/open-gate boundary.
  1298	
  1299	## Fix Policy
  1300	
  1301	If `--no-fix` was passed, do not edit.
  1302	
  1303	Otherwise apply the narrowest honest fix:
  1304	
  1305	1. Fix verified code bugs, broken reproduction commands, stale runner names,
  1306	   false PASS checks, and code/prose mismatches.
  1307	2. Demote overclaimed status when the artifact supports only support/bounded
  1308	   language.
  1309	3. Mark imported values explicitly; distinguish derived, conditional, fitted,
  1310	   measured, literature, boundary-condition, and insensitive nuisance inputs.
  1311	4. Add or repair paired runner/note references only when the artifact exists.
  1312	5. Make audit-system hygiene fixes only when they do not change the science:
  1313	   status-line tier labels, machine-local path removal, stale runner transcript
  1314	   refreshes, generated audit queue/ledger seeding, and discoverability wiring.
  1315	6. Rename ambiguous science shorthand to explicit repo vocabulary without
  1316	   changing the claim boundary. Examples: write `one-qubit operator algebra`
  1317	   (or equivalently `M_2(ℂ) ≅ Cl(3,0)`, `physical Cl(3) local algebra` as
  1318	   the real-algebra reading — all co-equal labels for the same retained
  1319	   algebra-isomorphism class), `Z^3 lattice`,
  1320	   `Koide Frobenius-equipartition condition`, or `Lie type A_1` instead of
  1321	   bare `A1` / `A2`.
  1322	7. Update `docs/repo/ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE.md` for live unresolved findings.
  1323	8. Route detailed resolved packets to
  1324	   `docs/work_history/repo/review_feedback/` only when a long packet is needed.
  1325	9. When a PR is non-landable but salvageable, preserve only the durable
  1326	   note/runner content, make the claim boundary canonical, and land that source
  1327	   salvage through the current requested landing path. If the rejected branch
  1328	   contains substantial non-source packet material, use a clean temporary
  1329	   worktree for integration, but do not create or open a follow-up PR.
  1330	
  1331	Skip:
  1332	
  1333	- nits;
  1334	- suspected findings without evidence;
  1335	- ambiguous science gaps that need new derivation;
  1336	- attempts to paper over missing theorem steps with confident prose;
  1337	- repo-wide axiom additions, new theory terminology, or new foundational
  1338	  premises that lack explicit user approval;
  1339	- broad refactors unrelated to the finding.
  1340	
  1341	## Audit-System Compatibility Gate
  1342	
  1343	This gate is mandatory when a branch adds or edits source notes, runners,
  1344	claim tables, lane stubs, or publication/control-plane files.
  1345	
  1346	The review loop must enforce the audit lane's propose/ratify split without
  1347	performing the independent audit:
  1348	
  1349	**Audit-hash churn guard.** Non-semantic hygiene sweeps on audited source notes
  1350	can be scientifically harmless while still invalidating large parts of the
  1351	audit ledger, because note hashes are source-content hashes. Before landing any
  1352	branch that touches many existing claim-note files for formatting, link-target,
  1353	path, vocabulary, or other non-science cleanup, run the pipeline in validation
  1354	mode and inspect the `seed_audit_ledger.py` / `invalidate_stale_audits.py`
  1355	counts. If the change would reset or requeue already-audited rows solely due to
  1356	non-semantic churn, do not land the broad source sweep. Either narrow the PR to
  1357	non-ledger/non-claim surfaces, land a reviewed hash/canonicalization tooling
  1358	repair first, or ask for explicit user approval to spend the audit capacity.
  1359	Never trade a clean audit graph for cosmetic source-note churn without making
  1360	that cost explicit.
  1361	
  1362	0. Before applying a PR, inventory any audit-status surface it touches:
  1363	
  1364	```bash
  1365	git diff --name-only <pr-base>..refs/tmp/pr-<N> -- \
  1366	  docs/audit/AUDIT_LEDGER.md docs/audit/AUDIT_QUEUE.md docs/audit/data \
  1367	  'docs/publication/ci3_z3/*_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md'
  1368	git diff <pr-base>..refs/tmp/pr-<N> -- docs/audit docs/publication/ci3_z3 \
  1369	  | grep -E 'audit_status|effective_status|audited_clean|audited_conditional|audited_failed|audited_renaming|audited_decoration|audited_numerical_match|previous_audits|audit_result|verdict'
  1370	```
  1371	
  1372	Treat this output as a provenance review, not as a merge recipe. Strip
  1373	PR-submitted generated ledgers, queues, effective-status tables, auditor
  1374	transcripts, and audit verdict payloads before landing. The only acceptable
  1375	audit-lane changes from a PR are reviewed source/tooling repairs and
  1376	machine-readable audit/re-audit targeting metadata, such as dispatcher
  1377	sidecars, that do not assert a verdict. After applying the source repair, run
  1378	the local pipeline to verify the row is queued or re-queued as intended, then
  1379	restore generated audit outputs from `origin/main` before committing. Pipeline
  1380	regeneration of `docs/audit/data/`, `docs/audit/AUDIT_LEDGER.md`,
  1381	`docs/audit/AUDIT_QUEUE.md`, `docs/audit/MISSING_DERIVATION_PROMPTS.md`, and
  1382	`docs/publication/ci3_z3/*_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md` is a VALIDATION step only;
  1383	framework PRs must never ship these files because the merge would overwrite
  1384	the audit lane's ratified state. The audit-loop run on `main` (nightly cron
  1385	plus `audit:` commits) is the sole channel for landing those outputs.
  1386	
  1387	1. Source-note `Status:` prose is not an audit authority. New or touched claim
  1388	   notes should use `Type:` / `Claim type:` metadata for intended audit
  1389	   classification.
  1390	2. If a no-go/firewall is intended to be theorem-grade, use
  1391	   `claim_type = no_go`; do not rely on support-style prose and expect audit
  1392	   ratification.
  1393	3. Keep disclaimers such as "This is not charged-lepton mass closure" outside
  1394	   audit metadata fields.
  1395	4. Do not prefill or recommend a verdict in author/review surfaces. Wording
  1396	   such as `target_audit_status: audited_clean`, `audit_status =
  1397	   audited_clean`, `effective_status = retained`, or "can land audited_clean"
  1398	   is not review-loop compatible. Use wording like `audit_status_authority:
  1399	   independent audit lane only` and "effective status is pipeline-derived
  1400	   after audit ratification and dependency closure."
  1401	5. Changed claim notes that cite load-bearing authorities must use markdown
  1402	   links, for example
  1403	   ``[`GRAPH_FIRST_SU3_INTEGRATION_NOTE.md`](GRAPH_FIRST_SU3_INTEGRATION_NOTE.md)``.
  1404	   Code-formatted names such as `` `GRAPH_FIRST_SU3_INTEGRATION_NOTE.md` `` do
  1405	   not seed graph dependencies and are not enough.
  1406	6. Run the audit pipeline after review fixes:
  1407	
  1408	```bash
  1409	bash docs/audit/scripts/run_pipeline.sh
  1410	python3 docs/audit/scripts/audit_lint.py --strict
  1411	git diff --check
  1412	```
  1413	
  1414	The known graph-cycle warning is acceptable. Any strict-lint error blocks a
  1415	review-loop PASS.
  1416	
  1417	**`note_hash` drift is a notice for non-retained rows, an error only for
  1418	retained-grade rows.** `note_hash` is a *source-content* hash, not an audit
  1419	verdict. When a review fix edits a claim note, its `note_hash` drifts from the
  1420	seeded value; `audit_lint.py` reports this drift as a non-blocking
  1421	`note_hash_drift_reaudit_pending` **notice** when the row is not retained-grade
  1422	(`unaudited` / `audited_conditional` / pending), because re-audit is simply
  1423	pending and the audit-lane re-seed refreshes the hash. Such a notice does **not**
  1424	block review-loop PASS and must **not** be "fixed" by committing audit-lane
  1425	ledger churn (that is the forbidden pipeline-output commit). A `note_hash`
  1426	mismatch on a **retained-grade** row (`retained` / `retained_bounded` /
  1427	`retained_no_go`) stays a hard **error**: an edited retained note laundered past
  1428	a stale ratification is a real integrity violation. Resolve it by re-auditing
  1429	(the audit lane re-seeds and archives the prior verdict) or by demoting the edit
  1430	per the audit-hash churn guard — never by refreshing the hash while keeping the
  1431	retained verdict.
  1432	
  1433	**Stuck-row repair requeue gate.** Terminal non-clean rows
  1434	(`audited_conditional` / `audited_renaming` / `audited_failed` /
  1435	`audited_numerical_match`) re-enter the audit queue only through their own
  1436	note or paired-runner hash drift, an upstream `deps_changed` invalidation, or
  1437	a dispatcher-sidecar re-audit target. Dependent-side edits never reschedule
  1438	the stuck row. When a branch's stated purpose is repairing such a row (the PR
  1439	title/body names the row or quotes its audit repair target):
  1440	
  1441	1. Verify the stuck row itself will requeue: its note or paired runner
  1442	   changes on the branch, or the branch ships dispatcher-sidecar targeting
  1443	   metadata naming the row.
  1444	2. If the audit-named repair is dependent-side only (for example, narrowing
  1445	   dependents' citing sentences to the audited scope), add a dated
  1446	   downstream-hygiene line to the stuck row's own note boundary as part of
  1447	   the landing: a one-line source-side record of what changed downstream
  1448	   (date + what was narrowed + PR number), with no grade or verdict
  1449	   language. The hash drift re-enters the row into the ordinary queue and
  1450	   the re-auditor (or second auditor) sees the recorded condition.
  1451	3. Run the validation pipeline and confirm the row is queued or re-queued as
  1452	   intended, then restore generated audit outputs per the
  1453	   pipeline-output-stripped gate below.
  1454	4. Repair-PR review checklist: the audit repair target is quoted verbatim
  1455	   (from `verdict_rationale` / `notes_for_re_audit_if_any`) in the PR body;
  1456	   a sibling-runner pin sweep was done before every note edit (grep
  1457	   `scripts/` for runners pinning the edited sentences); no authored grade
  1458	   language anywhere; no `docs/audit/data/` content beyond
  1459	   dispatcher-sidecar targeting metadata.
  1460	
  1461	7. **Pipeline-output-stripped PASS gate (hard).** After running the pipeline
  1462	   for validation, the framework PR must NOT land any pipeline-regenerated
  1463	   audit-lane or effective-status surface. The independent audit lane is the
  1464	   sole authority for these files; a framework PR that ships them creates a
  1465	   dual-source-of-truth and overwrites the audit lane's ratified state at
  1466	   merge. The following must hold for review-loop to issue PASS:
  1467	
  1468	```bash
  1469	# Must produce no output. Any change here means the working tree has
  1470	# pipeline-regenerated audit-lane outputs left over from validation;
  1471	# drop them (see below) before recommitting.
  1472	git status --porcelain docs/audit/AUDIT_LEDGER.md \
  1473	                       docs/audit/AUDIT_QUEUE.md \
  1474	                       docs/audit/data \
  1475	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/PUBLICATION_AUDIT_DIVERGENCE.md \
  1476	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/CLAIMS_TABLE_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
  1477	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/DERIVATION_ATLAS_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
  1478	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/PUBLICATION_MATRIX_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
  1479	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/FULL_CLAIM_LEDGER_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
  1480	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/USABLE_DERIVED_VALUES_INDEX_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
  1481	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/RESULTS_INDEX_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
  1482	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/QUANTITATIVE_SUMMARY_TABLE_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md \
  1483	                       docs/publication/ci3_z3/DERIVATION_VALIDATION_MAP_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md
  1484	```
  1485	
  1486	If this command prints any lines, BLOCK PASS and instruct the operator to
  1487	DROP the regenerated files before recommitting:
  1488	
  1489	```bash
  1490	git checkout origin/main -- docs/audit/data/ \
  1491	                            docs/audit/AUDIT_QUEUE.md \
  1492	                            docs/audit/MISSING_DERIVATION_PROMPTS.md \
  1493	                            'docs/publication/ci3_z3/*_EFFECTIVE_STATUS.md' \
  1494	                            docs/publication/ci3_z3/PUBLICATION_AUDIT_DIVERGENCE.md
  1495	git clean -fd -- docs/audit/data/
  1496	```
  1497	
  1498	The pipeline is run for VALIDATION only — to confirm the source repair is
  1499	ingested and the runner row is queued or re-queued as intended. The
  1500	audit-loop pipeline run on `main` (nightly cron + `audit:` commits) is the
  1501	sole channel for landing the regenerated outputs. Framework PRs that ship
  1502	these files force a destructive overwrite of ratified audit state at merge
  1503	time and have been an active source of broken-row regressions.
  1504	
  1505	8. **Repository-portable links PASS gate (hard).** Markdown link targets on
  1506	   branch-modified `.md` files must be repo-relative or web URLs. Absolute
  1507	   local paths such as `/Users/<name>/...`, `/home/<name>/...`,
  1508	   `/private/tmp/...`, `/tmp/...`, `/var/...`, `/opt/...`, or `file://...`
  1509	   inside a markdown link target are non-portable: they break for other
  1510	   developers, CI runners, fresh clones, and independent reviewers.
  1511	
  1512	```bash
  1513	# Must produce no output. Scans branch-modified markdown for local absolute
  1514	# paths inside markdown link targets.
  1515	git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- '*.md' \
  1516	  | xargs -I{} grep -nE '\]\((/Users/|/home/|/private/|/tmp/|/var/|/opt/|file://)' {} 2>/dev/null
  1517	```
  1518	
  1519	If this command prints lines for files the branch is already modifying for
  1520	source, runner, methodology, or review reasons, rewrite the offending link
  1521	targets before PASS. The usual mechanical fix is to preserve the display text
  1522	and replace the target with a `../` chain relative to the source file's
  1523	directory, e.g. in `docs/SOURCE_RESOLVED_FOO_NOTE.md` rewrite
  1524	`(/Users/me/Projects/Physics/scripts/foo.py)` to `(../scripts/foo.py)`.
  1525	
  1526	This gate prevents new non-portable links from landing; it is not a license for
  1527	large standalone cosmetic sweeps over audited claim notes. If the PR's only
  1528	purpose is to rewrite existing local-path links across many audited source
  1529	notes, apply the audit-hash churn guard above before landing any broad cleanup.
  1530	
  1531	9. **No-Go Discipline PASS gate (hard).** Before issuing review-loop PASS,
  1532	   identify any artifact on the branch that ships a negative claim:
  1533	
  1534	```bash
  1535	# Source notes whose claim_type is no_go, or whose Status / Type line
  1536	# names walls / open conditions / "conditional on" content
  1537	git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- 'docs/*NO_GO*.md' 'docs/*BOUNDED*.md' \
  1538	                                           'docs/*STRETCH_ATTEMPT*.md' \
  1539	                                           'docs/*OBSTRUCTION*.md'
  1540	# Audit-data shards whose verdict_rationale or claim_type record walls
  1541	git diff origin/main...HEAD -- docs/audit/data/ledger docs/audit/data/ledger_meta.json \
  1542	  | grep -E '"claim_type": "no_go"|"verdict_rationale".*wall|"verdict_rationale".*condition'
  1543	# Any source note touched on this branch whose body contains negative-claim shape
  1544	git diff origin/main...HEAD -- 'docs/*.md' \
  1545	  | grep -E 'structurally undecidable|no retained primitive|requires new axiom|cannot be derived from A_min|conditional on .* walls?'
  1546	```
  1547	
  1548	For every match, the NoGoDisciplineReviewer must output `PASS` (N1-N8 walk
  1549	complete and no failure condition hit) before review-loop issues PASS. A
  1550	`FAIL` from NoGoDisciplineReviewer blocks PASS regardless of how other
  1551	reviewers voted. An unscrutinized no-go that ships through review cements
  1552	the overclaim at audit time and forecloses investigation paths permanently.
  1553	
  1554	If NoGoDisciplineReviewer outputs FAIL, apply the narrowest honest fix per
  1555	Fix Policy step 2 (demote to a narrower honest claim that passes N1-N8) and
  1556	re-review. Do not weaken the gate to PASS the branch.
  1557	
  1558	This gate is independent of the Pipeline-clean PASS gate above; both must
  1559	pass for review-loop to issue PASS.
  1560	
  1561	10. **Math-runner independent-check PASS gate (hard).** Before issuing
  1562	review-loop PASS for any branch that changes a runner, proof script, numeric
  1563	constant, matrix construction, optimizer, expected value, or note formula,
  1564	record the independent math check used by `CodeRunnerReviewer`. At least one
  1565	check must not share the same implementation path as the changed runner:
  1566	manual formula derivation, symbolic/algebraic reduction, finite toy-case
  1567	enumeration, independent recomputation, or invariant/limit tests. A runner
  1568	that merely computes its own target and prints PASS is not a proof that the
  1569	formula is correct. If an issue was reopened because the runner's math was
  1570	wrong, treat the whole formula family as suspect until the changed expression
  1571	and any reused helpers are cross-checked.
  1572	
  1573	11. **Native-language PASS gate (hard).** Changed repo-facing text must use
  1574	controlled, native repo vocabulary. Run `scripts/vocab_lint.py --fix` on all
  1575	branch-modified files before landing, then inspect changed headings, metadata,
  1576	runner banners, claim scopes, table labels, and review comments for
  1577	branch-local/draft language that the linter cannot know about. PR-specific
  1578	labels, draft-branch vocabulary, campaign names, and noncanonical theory
  1579	phrases must be rewritten into repo-native language or explicitly deferred in
  1580	`docs/repo/ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE.md`; do not land them silently.
  1581	
  1582	The review loop must not run `docs/audit/scripts/apply_audit.py` and must not
  1583	write `audit_status`, `audited_clean`, or other audit verdicts. If the branch
  1584	introduces retained-grade `claim_type` rows, report those claim IDs in the
  1585	final report as requiring the independent audit worker.
  1586	When a source repair changes a note or runner for a previously audited row,
  1587	the local result is `note_hash`/runner-hash drift plus queue/dispatch
  1588	visibility for independent re-audit. For a non-retained row this drift is a
  1589	benign `note_hash_drift_reaudit_pending` notice (see the Audit-System
  1590	Compatibility Gate) — it does not block strict lint and must not be repaired by
  1591	committing ledger churn. For a retained-grade row the drift is a strict error
  1592	that must be resolved by re-audit, not laundered. In all cases, do not preserve,
  1593	copy, or author a fresh `previous_audits` entry, `audit_status`, or verdict
  1594	rationale from the PR branch; the independent audit lane (nightly cron +
  1595	`audit:` commits) is the sole channel that refreshes the hash and re-ratifies.
  1596	
  1597	After the pipeline, inspect the changed claim rows in
  1598	`docs/audit/data/audit_ledger.json`:
  1599	
  1600	- `claim_type` must match the intended class (`positive_theorem`,
  1601	  `bounded_theorem`, `no_go`, `open_gate`, `decoration`, or `meta`).
  1602	- `audit_status` must remain `unaudited` unless the branch is only carrying
  1603	  already-audited history from `origin/main`.
  1604	- `effective_status` must be pipeline-derived, not hand-authored.
  1605	- New theorem/no-go/bounded rows with declared load-bearing authorities must
  1606	  have non-empty `deps` matching the markdown-linked authorities.
  1607	- Dependencies asserted as retained-grade must currently have
  1608	  `effective_status` in `{retained, retained_bounded, retained_no_go}`. Open
  1609	  gates, `unaudited`, `audit_in_progress`, `retained_pending_chain`, and
  1610	  terminal non-clean audit statuses are blockers for retained-grade claims.
  1611	
  1612	Useful review-only inventory:
  1613	
  1614	```bash
  1615	python3 - <<'PY'
  1616	import json, subprocess
  1617	changed = set()
  1618	for cmd in (
  1619	    ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "HEAD"],
  1620	    ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--cached"],
  1621	):
  1622	    changed.update(subprocess.check_output(cmd, text=True).splitlines())
  1623	try:
  1624	    changed.update(subprocess.check_output(
  1625	        ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "origin/main...HEAD"], text=True
  1626	    ).splitlines())
  1627	except Exception:
  1628	    pass
  1629	rows=json.load(open("docs/audit/data/audit_ledger.json"))["rows"]
  1630	for cid,row in rows.items():
  1631	    if row.get("note_path") in changed:
  1632	        print(cid, row.get("claim_type"), row.get("audit_status"),
  1633	              row.get("effective_status"), row.get("deps"),
  1634	              row.get("note_path"))
  1635	PY
  1636	```
  1637	
  1638	If generated audit files conflict while integrating current `origin/main`, do
  1639	not hand-merge generated JSON/Markdown. Resolve source files, prefer the
  1640	current remote generated audit files, then rerun `run_pipeline.sh` and strict
  1641	lint so the generated surface is rebuilt from source.
  1642	
  1643	## Smoketest
  1644	
  1645	After fixes, run the smallest relevant checks:
  1646	
  1647	- `python3 -m py_compile <changed .py files>` for changed Python files;
  1648	- changed paired runners directly when they are expected to be short;
  1649	- for changed math-bearing runners, independently verify formulas/constants
  1650	  before trusting PASS output: compare note equations to code line by line,
  1651	  check signs/factors/normalizations, run a second implementation or symbolic
  1652	  simplification when practical, and add finite edge-case or invariant checks
  1653	  when they would have caught the suspected class of error;
  1654	- if many changed runners are part of the branch, execute all practical
  1655	  changed runners with a bounded timeout, then rerun any timeout once with a
  1656	  longer timeout before classifying it as slow rather than broken;
  1657	- any reproduction commands named in changed notes when practical;
  1658	- publication/control-plane consistency checks by reading changed tables and
  1659	  nearby authority surfaces.
  1660	- `bash docs/audit/scripts/run_pipeline.sh` and
  1661	  `python3 docs/audit/scripts/audit_lint.py --strict` when claim notes or
  1662	  governance/publication surfaces changed.
  1663	
  1664	If a runner is long, stochastic, or requires unavailable data, do not fake the
  1665	check. Report it as not run with the reason.
  1666	
  1667	## Re-Review Tracking
  1668	
  1669	Never re-review unchanged files.
  1670	
  1671	After each fix pass:
  1672	
  1673	1. Identify files modified by the fix pass.
  1674	2. If committing is allowed, create one iteration commit:
  1675	   `fix: address physics review findings (iteration N)`.
  1676	3. Set `files_to_review` to the files modified by the fix pass.
  1677	4. Add interacting files only if they are also in the original changed-file
  1678	   set. Find interactions through imports, runner/note pairs, canonical harness
  1679	   rows, publication tables, and explicit cross-links.
  1680	5. Loop until clean, no files changed, or max iterations reached.
  1681	
  1682	## Final Report
  1683	
  1684	Report:
  1685	
  1686	- iterations run;
  1687	- files reviewed;
  1688

  1733	## Author Pre-Flight (input hygiene)
  1734	
  1735	Authors are expected to run [`PREFLIGHT.md`](PREFLIGHT.md) before requesting
  1736	review. The pre-flight is authoring discipline, not a gate: it grants no
  1737	standing, replaces no reviewer lens, and its absence blocks nothing by
  1738	itself — but a reviewer may cite a skipped pre-flight item as a finding when
  1739	the defect it would have caught is present. Whether such findings are fixed
  1740	in place or the branch is rejected follows the existing Fix Policy and
  1741	close-with-reason path; the checklist adds no new disposition.
  1742	
  1743	## Arguments
  1744	
  1745	Parse:
  1746	
  1747	- focus text: optional free-text review focus;
  1748	- `--max-iterations N`: optional cap, default `5`;
  1749	- `--no-fix`: review only, do not edit;
  1750	- `--no-commit`: fix locally but do not create iteration commits.

  1752	## Setup
  1753	
  1754	1. Read the local review/governance surfaces before judging status:
  1755	   - `docs/repo/REVIEW_FEEDBACK_WORKFLOW.md`
  1756	   - `docs/repo/ACTIVE_REVIEW_QUEUE.md`
  1757	   - `docs/repo/CONTROLLED_VOCABULARY.md`
  1758	   - `docs/CANONICAL_HARNESS_INDEX.md`
  1759	   - `docs/audit/README.md`
  1760	   - `docs/ai_methodology/skills/PRIMITIVE_REGISTRY_CHECK.md`
  1761	   - `docs/audit/data/axiom_premise_nodes.json` and the source notes named by
  1762	     relevant primitive nodes
  1763	   - `docs/audit/data/premise_decision_history.json`
  1764	   - `docs/publication/ci3_z3/` when publication-facing files changed
  1765	   - `docs/publication/ci3_z3/USABLE_DERIVED_VALUES_INDEX.md` when
  1766	     quantitative or imported-value claims changed
  1767	2. Determine the base ref:
  1768	   - prefer `origin/main` if present;
  1769	   - otherwise use `main`;
  1770	   - if the current branch is the base branch, use `HEAD~1`.
  1771	3. Compute the review base with `git merge-base HEAD <base-ref>`.
  1772	4. Build the original changed-file set from committed, staged, unstaged, and
  1773	   untracked changes. Do not review outside this set except interacting files
  1774	   that are also in this original set.
  1775	5. Record whether the worktree was initially clean. If it was dirty, do not
  1776	   auto-commit without explicit user permission unless the slash-command
  1777	   invocation clearly requested commit-producing fixes.
  1778	6. If the task is to review open/non-landed PRs, include all non-merged,
  1779	   non-draft PRs in the requested scope except PRs the user explicitly
  1780	   excluded. Draft PRs are out of scope: ignore them entirely and do not land
  1781	   them unless the user explicitly asks to inspect a draft PR without landing
  1782	   it. Closed-but-unmerged PR heads can be inspected with `gh pr view` and
  1783	   `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:refs/tmp/pr-<N>`.
  1784	
  1785	Useful commands:
  1786	
  1787	```bash
  1788	git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD
  1789	git diff --name-only --cached
  1790	git diff --name-only
  1791	git ls-files --others --exclude-standard
  1792	git diff <base>...HEAD -- <files>
  1793	git diff --cached -- <files>
  1794	git diff -- <files>
  1795	```
  1796	
  1797	For untracked files, include their full content or a concise new-file summary
  1798	in reviewer prompts.

  1800	## Stale PR Integration Guard
  1801	
  1802	When landing one or more PRs, protect already-landed science before applying
  1803	any branch content. A PR branch may be based before another PR just landed, so
  1804	checking out whole files from that stale PR head can erase current-main source
  1805	science in shared files.
  1806	
  1807	For every PR before integration:
  1808	
  1809	```bash
  1810	git fetch origin main pull/<N>/head:refs/tmp/pr-<N>
  1811	pr_base=$(git merge-base origin/main refs/tmp/pr-<N>)
  1812	comm -12 \
  1813	  <(git diff --name-only "$pr_base"..origin/main | sort) \
  1814	  <(git diff --name-only "$pr_base"..refs/tmp/pr-<N> | sort)
  1815	```
  1816	
  1817	If the overlap list is non-empty, or if earlier PRs have landed during the
  1818	same review-loop run, do **not** run `git checkout refs/tmp/pr-<N> -- <file>`
  1819	for those paths. Integrate the PR's delta against its merge base with a
  1820	three-way patch, rebase/merge, or cherry-pick source commits, then resolve any
  1821	conflicts by preserving both current-main science and the salvageable PR
  1822	science:
  1823	
  1824	```bash
  1825	git diff --binary "$pr_base"..refs/tmp/pr-<N> -- <source paths> > /tmp/pr<N>.patch
  1826	git apply --3way /tmp/pr<N>.patch
  1827	```
  1828	
  1829	Whole-file checkout from a PR head is allowed only when the file is new on the
  1830	PR or when `git diff --quiet "$pr_base"..origin/main -- <file>` proves current
  1831	`main` has not changed that path since the PR base. For every overlapped
  1832	source path, do a science-loss guard after integration: the current-main diff
  1833	from `pr_base` to `origin/main` must still be represented in the final file.
  1834	If that cannot be verified quickly, stop and treat it as a blocking integration
  1835	hazard rather than risking science loss.
  1836	
  1837	Generated audit JSON/Markdown is a special case: do not hand-merge generated
  1838	files from stale PR heads. Resolve source files first, prefer the current
  1839	`origin/main` generated audit surface, then rerun the audit pipeline and strict
  1840	lint to regenerate it.
  1841	
  1842	## Reviewer Fanout
  1843	
  1844	On each iteration, set `files_to_review` to the files that changed since their
  1845	last clean review. On iteration 1, use all original changed files.
  1846	
  1847	Run every applicable reviewer lens. Under the shared-pool concurrency
  1848	budget (Default Entry above), combine the lenses into one or two passes per
  1849	PR — full per-lens parallel fanout through the available agent/subagent
  1850	mechanism is the quiet-pool mode. If parallel agents are unavailable, run
  1851	the same reviewer passes locally and report that limitation. In every mode,
  1852	each applicable lens must be explicitly covered and named in the findings.
  1853	
  1854	### Required Reviewers
  1855	
  1856	- `CodeRunnerReviewer`
  1857	  Review changed Python/scripts/log-producing code. Check syntax, decisive
  1858	  assertions, hard-coded targets, stale fixtures, literal `True` checks,
  1859	  hidden observations, reproducibility, paired runner/output agreement, and
  1860	  whether the runner actually tests the note's load-bearing bridge. If a
  1861	  runner checks audit-ledger dependency status, it must use the current
  1862	  retained-grade set (`retained`, `retained_bounded`, `retained_no_go`) rather
  1863	  than hard-coding stale expectations such as exactly `retained`.
  1864	  For math-bearing runners, PASS output is not enough. Extract every
  1865	  load-bearing formula, sign, factor, normalization, matrix identity,
  1866	  optimizer objective, and expected numeric value from the changed code and
  1867	  note, then verify them by an independent route before landing: manual
  1868	  derivation against the note, symbolic simplification, small-case exhaustive
  1869	  enumeration, a second implementation that does not share the same expression,
  1870	  or invariant/limit/property checks. Treat self-confirming tests, expected
  1871	  values generated by the same implementation under review, missing factor/sign
  1872	  checks, or stale reopened bug reports as blocking until the formula is
  1873	  corrected or the claim is demoted to a narrower supported boundary.
  1874	
  1875	- `PhysicsClaimReviewer`
  1876	  Attack theorem notes, claims tables, publication surfaces, and prose. Check
  1877	  semantic bridges, selector assumptions, status labels, exact/bounded/support
  1878	  boundaries, and code/prose drift.
  1879	
  1880	- `ImportSupportReviewer`
  1881	  Inventory every measured, fitted, literature, PDG, cosmological,
  1882	  normalization, boundary-condition, or convention input. Classify each as
  1883	  `zero-input structural`, `framework-derived`, `one computed lattice input`,
  1884	  `explicit normalization/boundary condition`, `standard/literature
  1885	  correction`, `observational comparator`, `support-only`, `insensitive
  1886	  nuisance`, or `unjustified import`. For a Nature-grade retention claim, every
  1887	  import must be derived, disclosed as a non-satisfying condition with a narrow role, quantitatively
  1888	  insensitive, or the claim must be demoted.
  1889	
  1890	- `NatureRetentionReviewer`
  1891	  Apply the hostile external-review bar. Ask whether the result can honestly
  1892	  be called retained/Nature-grade: no hidden unit identification, no structural
  1893	  redefinition, no imported selector, no unsupported first-principles claim,
  1894	  no unmatched observed target, and clear falsifiers/open gates. Output
  1895	  `RETAINED`, `RETAINED SUPPORT`, `BOUNDED`, `OPEN`, `NO-GO`, or `REJECT`.
  1896	
  1897	- `NoGoDisciplineReviewer`
  1898	  Scrutinize negative claims with the same rigor as positive ones. Trigger
  1899	  this reviewer whenever changed content includes a `no_go`, `stretch_attempt`,
  1900	  `bounded_with_named_walls`, or derived-no-go-boundary artifact, or when any
  1901	  other reviewer in this fanout outputs `NO-GO` / `BOUNDED` / `OVERCLAIM` on
  1902	  a negative claim. The reviewer must invoke the `no-go-discipline` skill
  1903	  and walk N1-N8 against the branch content (see
  1904	  [`docs/ai_methodology/skills/no-go-discipline/SKILL.md`](../no-go-discipline/SKILL.md)):
  1905	  N1 alternative-route enumeration (≥5 distinct routes), N2
  1906	  wall-independence audit, N3 hidden-wall scan, N4 residual matching,
  1907	  N5 rhetoric audit (per-element / per-mode / per-block / lattice-wide
  1908	  resolutions), N6 partial-closure path scan (convention-reframe vs new
  1909	  axiom), N7 steelman, N8 cross-cycle echo. Output `PASS` (negative claim
  1910	  honestly scoped) or `FAIL` with the failing checklist items named and the
  1911	  narrowest demoted claim proposed (`partial-attempt-with-named-untested-routes`,
  1912	  `partial-narrowing`, `bounded-with-corrected-wall-count`, or
  1913	  `stretch-attempt-with-honest-residual`). The reviewer must not approve a
  1914	  no-go that has not been stress-tested against the framework's full
  1915	  authority surface — under-tested negative claims are at least as harmful
  1916	  as overclaimed positive ones because they foreclose investigation paths
  1917	  permanently.
  1918	
  1919	- `LabelingConventionReviewer`
  1920	  Detect labeling/naming/convention content masquerading as a bounded
  1921	  theorem. Trigger whenever changed content includes a `bounded_theorem`
  1922	  candidate whose load-bearing claim is a labeling/naming/convention
  1923	  statement (parallel to the u/c/t mass-ordering convention or the
  1924	  e/μ/τ charged-lepton naming) rather than an algebraic claim with
  1925	  explicit named conditions. A labeling convention has no propositional
  1926	  premise content, so `retained_bounded` grade does not apply — the
  1927	  grade is for algebraic claims with explicit named premises, not for
  1928	  stipulations about names.
  1929	
  1930	  The right outcome is to split:
  1931	- files reviewed;
  1932	- total findings, fixed findings, skipped findings;
  1933	- import/support inventory summary;
  1934	- final claim-strength disposition;
  1935	- audit-compatibility status and proposed claim IDs needing independent audit;
  1936	- commits created;
  1937	- checks run and checks skipped;
  1938	- remaining issues with disposition;
  1939	- recommendation: `PASS`, `PASS WITH BOUNDED CLAIMS`, or `NEEDS MANUAL SCIENCE`.
  1940	
  1941	Do not claim Nature readiness. Say whether the branch meets this repo's
  1942	Nature-grade retention bar or exactly what remains open.

  2001	
  2002	# No-Go Discipline
  2003	
  2004	## Skill Freshness
  2005	
  2006	Before applying this skill, perform the repo skill freshness check described in
  2007	`docs/ai_methodology/skills/SKILL_FRESHNESS_CHECK.md`. If a newer version of
  2008	this `SKILL.md` exists on `origin/main`, follow that version for the current
  2009	task.
  2010	
  2011	A structured gate for negative claims. The symmetric counterpart of the V1-V5
  2012	Promotion Value Gate in `physics-loop` — V1-V5 prevents overclaiming positives;
  2013	N1-N8 prevents overclaiming negatives.
  2014	
  2015	Agents are good at finding one route that fails. They are bad at proving all
  2016	routes fail. This skill makes that gap explicit and gates negative-claim output
  2017	on a structured stress-test before the claim can ship.
  2018	
  2019	## When to invoke
  2020	
  2021	Invoke this skill **before shipping** any cycle artifact, PR body, source note,
  2022	runner, or review verdict that asserts:
  2023	
  2024	- a `no_go` result ("structurally closed," "no route exists," "no retained
  2025	  primitive supplies this");
  2026	- a `stretch_attempt_negative` outcome ("the attempted route does not close");
  2027	- a `bounded_with_named_walls` result ("conditional on N open conditions/walls");
  2028	- a derived no-go boundary inside a positive theorem ("the per-element
  2029	  identity does not lift");
  2030	- an audit-conditional verdict rationale that names a residual wall.
  2031	
  2032	Skills that must invoke this gate before approving negative-claim output:
  2033	
  2034	- `physics-loop` — before any cycle classified `no_go` / `stretch_negative` /
  2035	  `bounded_with_walls` can ship to a PR;
  2036	- `review-loop` — when any reviewer reports an OVERCLAIM on a negative claim,
  2037	  or before a `NO-GO` / `BOUNDED` recommendation is finalized;
  2038	- `audit-loop` — before issuing `audited_clean` for a `claim_type: no_go`
  2039	  row, or any verdict whose rationale names walls (independent audit
  2040	  authority; this gate prevents the audit lane from inheriting the
  2041	  source-note's overclaim);
  2042	- any future skill that produces negative-claim output.
  2043	
  2044	## The N1-N8 checklist
  2045	
  2046	Each item must be answered IN WRITING in the cycle's `CLAIM_STATUS_CERTIFICATE.md`
  2047	(or in a dedicated `NO_GO_DISCIPLINE_CHECKLIST.md`) before the negative claim
  2048	can ship. The checklist must be visible in the PR body or review verdict so
  2049	the audit lane and reviewers can see exactly what was tested.
  2050	
  2051	### N1 — Alternative route enumeration
  2052	
  2053	Name at least **5 distinct attack routes** against the claim being declared
  2054	closed. For each route, give:
  2055	
  2056	- one-sentence statement of what the route would attempt;
  2057	- one-sentence statement of why the route fails (with retained-authority
  2058	  citation);
  2059	- honesty marker: `ATTEMPTED` (tested in this cycle) or `RULED OUT BY PRIOR`
  2060	  (closed by an existing retained authority — cite it).
  2061	
  2062	**Failure condition:** if you can name fewer than 5 distinct routes, the
  2063	no-go is premature. List what you can and stop; do not ship.
  2064	
  2065	**Why 5:** small enough to be achievable in one cycle, large enough to force
  2066	agents off the "I tried one obvious route" failure mode that produced three
  2067	out of four overclaims in the v-scale-planck-convention campaign (see
  2068	[`references/case-studies.md`](references/case-studies.md)).
  2069	
  2070	### N2 — Wall-independence audit
  2071	
  2072	If claiming multiple walls / open conditions / load-bearing conditionals, produce
  2073	a pairwise table. For each pair `(W_i, W_j)`:
  2074	
  2075	- does closing `W_i` automatically close `W_j`? (yes / no);
  2076	- does closing `W_j` automatically close `W_i`? (yes / no);
  2077	- independent? (only if both above are no).
  2078	
  2079	Collapse all pairs where one wall follows from another. The claim must use
  2080	the **collapsed** wall set, not the inflated raw set.
  2081	
  2082	**Failure condition:** if the pairwise table shows any wall follows from
  2083	another but the source-note still presents them as independent, the
  2084	claim is overstated and must be narrowed.
  2085	
  2086	### N3 — Hidden-wall scan
  2087	
  2088	Re-read your own proof. Search for these phrases and any close variants:
  2089	
  2090	- "we assume";
  2091	- "by construction";
  2092	- "as is standard";
  2093	- "the framework provides";
  2094	- "bridge context";
  2095	- "background";
  2096	- "naturally";
  2097	- "obviously";
  2098	- "standard QFT";
  2099	- "registered" / "canonical".
  2100	
  2101	For each hit, classify:
  2102	
  2103	- cited retained authority (with link) — keep as-is;
  2104	- hidden condition — **promote to explicit wall** and re-run N2;
  2105	- genuine non-load-bearing context — annotate that it is non-load-bearing.
  2106	
  2107	**Failure condition:** any hidden condition promoted to a wall means the
  2108	wall count was wrong; revise the claim.
  2109	
  2110	### N4 — Residual matching
  2111	
  2112	For every prior no-go / wall / campaign cited as a witness against the
  2113	current claim, verify the **residual matches exactly**. Build a per-citation
  2114	table:
  2115	
  2116	- cited witness (file path, line);
  2117	- residual the witness attacks (named explicitly);
  2118	- residual you are claiming closed (named explicitly);
  2119	- match? (yes / no).
  2120	
  2121	Drop every citation where the residuals differ. Recount your witness
  2122	support after dropping non-matches.
  2123	
  2124	**Failure condition:** if dropping non-matching citations reduces the witness
  2125	count below what the claim needs, the claim is unsupported.
  2126	
  2127	### N5 — Rhetoric audit
  2128	
  2129	Any phrase of the form "X is not a Y-fact" must be checked at multiple
  2130	resolutions. Specifically, for each such phrase, list:
  2131	
  2132	- per-element / per-site / per-mode / per-block / lattice-wide versions;
  2133	- which resolutions you actually tested;
  2134	- whether the negative result holds at the resolutions you did NOT test.
  2135	
  2136	If "X is not a per-element Y-fact" was proven but "X is not a per-mode
  2137	Y-fact" was not tested, the broader phrase is over-broad and must be narrowed.
  2138	
  2139	**Failure condition:** any over-broad phrase that has not been verified at
  2140	every named resolution must be replaced with the narrowest accurate phrase.
  2141	
  2142	### N6 — Partial-closure path scan
  2143	
  2144	Per `feedback_no_new_axioms.md`, the legitimate import-bearing shape is
  2145	(1) take an explicit import; (2) bound-theorem; (3) retire-import audit. A
  2146	labeling convention, meta-ratification, or definition refactor that closes
  2147	the wall WITHOUT new physics is NOT a new axiom — it is the import-retirement
  2148	path.
  2149	
  2150	Also separate approved framework primitives from walls. A primitive already
  2151	registered in `docs/audit/data/axiom_premise_nodes.json`, such as the
  2152	scale-reference or kinetic-isotropy primitive, chain-satisfies dependencies
  2153	without making the claim bounded. The kinetic-isotropy primitive supplies only
  2154	structural OS0 kinetic-form isotropy `c_t = c_s`, not dynamics or a
  2155	Lorentz-closure theorem. A proposed but unapproved primitive has zero premise
  2156	weight until explicit approval; it is not an automatic no-go wall.
  2157	Run `docs/ai_methodology/skills/PRIMITIVE_REGISTRY_CHECK.md` before writing
  2158	"no retained primitive supplies this" or any equivalent wall language.
  2159	
  2160	Before declaring "this requires a new axiom," scan for:
  2161	
  2162	- existing reframings that move the wall from "physics" to "convention";
  2163	- existing meta-notes / interpretation-stance notes;
  2164	- existing controlled-vocabulary entries that name the residual as
  2165	  labeling-only;
  2166	- existing PRs in flight that propose convention ratification.
  2167	
  2168	For each candidate path found, report: file path, status, what it would close.
  2169	
  2170	**Failure condition:** if you found a partial-closure path that closes the
  2171	wall via convention/reframe (not new physics) but the no-go still calls
  2172	this "new axiom required," the no-go is misclassified.
  2173	
  2174	### N7 — Steelman
  2175	
  2176	Write the **strongest possible one-paragraph argument AGAINST your own
  2177	no-go.** Use a hostile reviewer voice. Name the specific route or framing
  2178	that might break the claim. Cite the strongest authority that supports the
  2179	counter-argument.
  2180	
  2181	If you can write a convincing steelman, the no-go is premature: there is
  2182	at least one route you have not closed. Demote to partial-attempt and ship
  2183	the steelman as the next cycle's target.
  2184	
  2185	If you cannot write a steelman after honest effort, the no-go is solid.
  2186	
  2187	**Failure condition:** failing to produce a steelman because "I can't think
  2188	of any counter-argument" usually means you have not tried — not that no
  2189	counter-argument exists. Try harder; if still nothing, the no-go is solid.
  2190	
  2191	### N8 — Cross-cycle echo
  2192	
  2193	Search the repo for prior cycles, notes, or campaigns that named **similar**
  2194	walls (not necessarily identical — similar shape).
  2195	
  2196	- `grep -rln "structurally undecidable\|no retained primitive\|requires new axiom\|cannot be derived from A_min" docs/`;
  2197	- walks of `NO_GO_LEDGER.md` files under `.claude/science/physics-loops/`.
  2198	
  2199	For each prior wall:
  2200	
  2201	- has it since been retired? (via reframe / ratification / convention /
  2202	  new authority);
  2203	- if yes: by what mechanism? Could the same mechanism apply to YOUR wall?
  2204	
  2205	**Failure condition:** if a structurally similar prior wall was retired
  2206	by a mechanism that you have not considered applying to your current wall,
  2207	the no-go is premature.
  2208	
  2209	## Output
  2210	
  2211	A `NO_GO_DISCIPLINE_CHECKLIST.md` (or a `## No-Go Discipline Gate` section
  2212	in `CLAIM_STATUS_CERTIFICATE.md`) recording the answers to N1-N8 verbatim.
  2213	The output must be present in the PR body or review verdict.
  2214	
  2215	Status: `PASS` if all 8 checks have answers and no failure conditions are
  2216	hit. `FAIL` if any failure condition is hit.
  2217	
  2218	## Stop conditions
  2219	
  2220	If the gate produces `FAIL`:
  2221	
  2222	1. Do not ship the negative claim as currently framed.
  2223	2. Demote to one of: `partial-attempt-with-named-untested-routes`,
  2224	   `partial-narrowing`, `bounded-with-corrected-wall-count`, or
  2225	   `stretch-attempt-with-honest-residual`.
  2226	3. Record the failing checklist items in `NO_GO_LEDGER.md`.
  2227	4. Either (a) attempt the missed routes in the same cycle if budget allows,
  2228	   or (b) ship the narrowed claim and queue the missed routes for the next
  2229	   cycle.
  2230	
  2231	If the gate produces `PASS`:
  2232	
  2233	- ship the negative claim with the checklist visible in the PR body or
  2234	  review verdict;
  2235	- the independent audit lane and other reviewers can then see exactly what
  2236	  was tested and what alternative routes were closed.
  2237	
  2238	## Case studies
  2239	
  2240	Three archetypal failure modes drawn from the 2026-05-10 v-scale-planck-convention
  2241	campaign are recorded in
  2242	[`references/case-studies.md`](references/case-studies.md). Each is a real
  2243	example of a negative claim that shipped without this discipline and was
  2244	later caught by a stress-test review.
  2245	
  2246	The cases illustrate:
  2247	
  2248	- **F1 — Untested alternative route** (cycle 4 / G4 γ-norm overclaim):
  2249	  per-element identity tested, per-mode route via Matsubara product
  2250	  structure not tested, but the conclusion was phrased as universal.
  2251	- **F2 — Independent walls that are not independent, plus hidden walls**
  2252	  (cycle 3 / T1 three-wall decomposition): one wall was downstream of
  2253	  another; a fourth wall was buried as "bridge context."
  2254	- **F3 — Conflated residuals plus dismissed partial-closure path**
  2255	  (cycle 1 / substep-4 ratchet): BAE 30-probe synthesis cited as witness
  2256	  against species-identification AC_φλ when the residuals differ;
  2257	  existing meta-conventions ratification path dismissed as "new axiom."
  2258	
  2259	## Relationship to other skills
  2260	
  2261	- `physics-loop` V1-V5 Promotion Value Gate prevents overclaiming POSITIVE
  2262	  results. N1-N8 prevents overclaiming NEGATIVE results. They are
  2263	  symmetric and independently mandatory.
  2264	- `physics-loop` `NO_GO_LEDGER.md` is where failed routes are recorded for
  2265	  future campaigns. N1-N8 output gets appended there when a cycle ships a
  2266	  negative claim.
  2267	- `physics-loop` Deep Work Rules' stretch-attempt valid-output language
  2268	  ("a valid output may be partial structure, a sharper obstruction, a
  2269	  falsified premise, or a worked failed derivation with the exact
  2270	  load-bearing wall named") aligns with the demotion options here.
  2271	- `review-loop` adds a `NoGoDisciplineReviewer` that invokes N1-N8 when
  2272	  reviewing changes that ship negative claims.
  2273	- `audit-loop` should invoke N1-N8 before issuing `audited_conditional`
  2274	  verdicts that name walls.
  2275	
  2276	## Non-Negotiables
  2277	
  2278	- N1 requires 5 distinct routes, not 5 phrasings of the same route.
  2279	- N7 steelman must be the strongest counter-argument, not a token paragraph.
  2280	- N6 "convention reframe vs new axiom" distinction must respect
  2281	  `feedback_no_new_axioms.md` — bounded condition with named import-retirement
  2282	  audit is the legitimate path, approved primitives are not bounded walls, and
  2283	  proposed new primitives require explicit approval rather than
  2284	  silent use or automatic foreclosure.
  2285	- Do not weaken the gate by lowering the failure thresholds. If a cycle
  2286	  cannot pass N1-N8, the negative claim is not yet ready to ship; that is
  2287	  the gate working correctly.
  2288	- This gate does not prevent shipping; it prevents OVERCLAIMING. A correctly
  2289	  scoped narrow no-go passes N1-N8 by being narrow.
  2290	- This gate is also not a substitute for honest physics work. Passing N1-N8
  2291	  on a real no-go just records the discipline; the no-go itself stands or
  2292	  falls on its science content.

  3183	    34	declared a scalar fiber and named matrix-valued (internal-component)

  3185	    36	that item — and something sharper than an envelope at its core: an
  3186	    37	**exact identity** for the norm of a fiber pair term. For any
  3187	    38	`n_f × n_f` matrix `k`,
  3188	    39	
  3189	    40	> `|| Σ_ab k_ab c_{xa}^† c_{yb} + h.c. || = ||k||_{S1}`  (`x ≠ y`),

  3196	    47	`n_f`, with `n_f = 1` recovering the sibling exactly. The CT note's

  3206	    57	and JW computational realization of the fermionic siblings; a supplied

  3208	    59	bound `||k_xy||_op ≤ K e^{−η||x−y||_∞}` (`K`, `η` background- and
  3209	    60	volume-independent where the sibling's source supplies that);
  3210	    61	`0 < mu < η/3` as in the sibling. The second-quantized family: pair
  3211	    62	terms `h_{xy} = Σ_ab (k_xy)_{ab} c_{xa}^† c_{yb} + h.c.` (`x ≠ y`) and
  3212	    63	on-site terms `h_x = Σ_ab (k_xx)_{ab} c_{xa}^† c_{xb}` (`k_xx`

  3218	    69	## Results
  3219	    70	
  3220	    71	**Pair trace-norm lemma (exact identity, rebuilt).** Let `x ≠ y` and
  3221	    72	`k` any `n_f × n_f` complex matrix, `T = Σ_ab k_ab c_{xa}^† c_{yb}`.
  3222	    73	Write the singular value decomposition `k = U Σ V^†` with singular
  3223	    74	values `σ_1, …, σ_{n_f}`. Define rotated modes `C_{x,i}^† =
  3224	    75	Σ_a U_{ai} c_{xa}^†` and `C_{y,i} = Σ_b (V^†)_{ib} c_{yb}` — both are
  3225	    76	particle-conserving unitary mode rotations, which preserve the CAR
  3226	    77	(gated at an instance). Then
  3227	    78	
  3228	    79	> `T = Σ_i σ_i C_{x,i}^† C_{y,i}`,  so
  3229	    80	> `T + T^† = Σ_i σ_i (C_{x,i}^† C_{y,i} + h.c.)`,
  3230	    81	
  3231	    82	a sum of Hermitian hop terms on **disjoint** mode pairs: they commute
  3232	    83	(the graded lemma of the fermionic sibling — even, disjoint), each has
  3233	    84	spectrum `{−σ_i, 0, +σ_i}` (gated), and commuting Hermitian operators
  3234	    85	with disjoint mode supports have joint spectrum equal to sums, so
  3235	    86	
  3236	    87	> `||T + T^†|| = Σ_i σ_i = ||k||_{S1}`.
  3237	    88	
  3238	    89	Gated on seven exact instances spanning rank-one, diagonal, unitary,
  3239	    90	and **non-normal** fiber matrices (e.g. `k = [[2,1],[0,1]]`: both
  3240	    91	sides `√10`; `k = I_2`: both sides `2` — which already shows the
  3241	    92	operator norm alone, `1`, is NOT the answer).
  3242	    93	
  3243	    94	**On-site bound (with strictness and saturation exhibits).** For
  3244	    95	Hermitian `k` with eigenvalues `λ_i`, the on-site term
  3245	    96	`h_x = Σ k_ab c_{xa}^† c_{xb}` diagonalizes to `Σ λ_i n_i`; its
  3246	    97	spectrum is the subset sums of `{λ_i}`, so
  3247	    98	
  3248	    99	> `||h_x|| = max(Σ_{λ_i>0} λ_i, −Σ_{λ_i<0} λ_i) ≤ ||k||_{S1}`,
  3249	   100	
  3250	   101	with strict inequality at `k = diag(1, −1)` (norm `1 < 2`) and
  3251	   102	equality at `k = diag(1, 2)` (norm `3`) — both gated.
  3252	   103	
  3253	   104	**Fiber-dimension envelope.** `||k||_{S1} = Σσ_i ≤ n_f · σ_max =
  3254	   105	n_f ||k||_op` (gated, with equality at the identity fiber — the
  3255	   106	exhibit that the envelope is attained and cannot be improved without
  3256	   107	more kernel data).
  3257	   108	
  3258	   109	**Theorem (the fiber feed).** With the supplied operator-norm kernel
  3259	   110	bound, the lemma and envelope give `||h_{xy}|| = ||k_xy||_{S1} ≤
  3260	   111	n_f K e^{−η r}` and `||h_x|| ≤ n_f K`; every step of the sibling
  3261	   112	scalar feed then multiplies by `n_f`:
  3262	   113	
  3263	   114	> `κ_U ≤ κ̄_fiber = n_f · [K + 8K·x(13+10x+x²)/(1−x)³]`,
  3264	   115	> `x = e^{−(η−3mu)}`,
  3265	   116	
  3266	   117	for every `mu < η/3` — at `x = 1/2` the envelope evaluates to exactly
  3267	   118	`585·n_f·K` (gated) — and the block07 display applies verbatim, with
  3268	   119	the uniform corollary intact: `n_f` is part of the supplied geometry,
  3269	   120	identical across backgrounds, so background-uniformity carries
  3270	   121	unchanged. Setting `n_f = 1` recovers the sibling's scalar feed
  3271	   122	exactly (consistency gate). **Sharper-data remark:** a kernel supplied
  3272	   123	directly with trace-norm decay (`||k_xy||_{S1} ≤ K' e^{−ηr}`) feeds
  3273	   124	with `K'` and no `n_f` factor — the factor is the price of op-norm
  3274	   125	data only (stated, not developed).

  3445	    59	## Hypotheses (all supplied, none derived)
  3446	    60	
  3447	    61	The supplied objects: (i) the CT note's kernel bound at fixed
  3448	    62	background — `||<x|h[U]|y>|| ≤ K e^{−η||x−y||_∞}` with `K =
  3449	    63	Const(m,d)`, `η = gamma_CT`, both independent of `U` and of volume
  3450	    64	(cited on that note's own surface, with its own provenance and audit
  3451	    65	status; **not re-proved here** — the Combes-Thomas argument is that
  3452	    66	note's content); (ii) the CAR algebra and second-quantization
  3453	    67	conventions of the fermionic siblings (JW realization as the
  3454	    68	computational device); (iii) a supplied `mu` with `0 < mu <
  3455	    69	gamma_CT/3`; (iv) the block07 class definition and theorem, cited
  3456	    70	where natively gated. The second-quantized family is: for unordered
  3457	    71	pairs `{x, y}`, `x ≠ y`:
  3458	    72	
  3459	    73	> `h_{xy} = <x|h[U]|y> c_x^† c_y + <y|h[U]|x> c_y^† c_x`
  3460	    74	
  3461	    75	(Hermitian since the kernel matrix is), and on-site terms
  3462	    76	`h_x = <x|h[U]|x> c_x^† c_x`. Every term is **even** (two generators),
  3463	    77	so the block07 even-CAR form applies. **What the many-body object
  3464	    78	is, precisely (review-sharpened):** the theorem below concerns the
  3465	    79	second-quantized BILINEAR `H[U] = Σ_{x,y} <x|h[U]|y> c_x^† c_y` built
  3466	    80	from the supplied kernel — unconditionally. The further identification
  3467	    81	of this bilinear with the many-body log-transfer generator holds ONLY
  3468	    82	under an explicit additional supplied hypothesis, stated as such: a
  3469	    83	positive, number-conserving **Gaussian factorization**
  3470	    84	`T_MB[U] = C(U)·Γ(T_1[U])` with scalar `C(U) > 0` (then
  3471	    85	`−log T_MB = −log C(U)·1 + dΓ(−log T_1)`, and the scalar term is an
  3472	    86	identity shift that drops from every commutator — gated). A
  3473	    87	one-particle kernel alone does NOT imply the factorization (review
  3474	    88	counterexample: `Γ(e^{−h})·e^{−g n_1 n_2}` has the same one-particle
  3475	    89	restriction but a quartic log). Without the factorization hypothesis,
  3476	    90	only the bilinear theorem is claimed. The kernel here is treated with
  3477	    91	a **scalar fiber**; matrix-valued (internal-component) kernels need a
  3478	    92	fiber-dimension envelope, named open. The axioms supply no dynamics (needled). Workhorse disclosure: one Opus 4.8 max-effort verification
  3479	    93	worker (owner-directed substitution under the workhorse skill) checked
  3480	    94	the assembly line-by-line against supervisor ground truth recorded
  3481	    95	first in the loop pack; the runner gates everything natively.

  3483	    97	## Results
  3484	    98	
  3485	    99	**Term norms and parity (gated in the JW representation).**
  3486	   100	`||c_x^† c_y|| = 1` for `x ≠ y` and `||c_x^† c_x|| = 1` (partial
  3487	   101	isometries; exact operator norms gated), so by the triangle
  3488	   102	inequality
  3489	   103	
  3490	   104	> `||h_{xy}|| ≤ 2 |<x|h[U]|y>| ≤ 2K e^{−η||x−y||_∞}`,  `||h_x|| ≤ K`,
  3491	   105	
  3492	   106	and every term is even and Hermitian (gated).
  3493	   107	
  3494	   108	**Metric conversion and shell count (exact).** On `Z^3`:
  3495	   109	`||z||_1 ≤ 3 ||z||_∞` (per-coordinate: each of the three coordinates
  3496	   110	is at most the maximum; gated by enumeration with equality attained on
  3497	   111	the diagonal), so `e^{mu||z||_1} ≤ e^{3mu||z||_∞}`; and the `l_∞`
  3498	   112	sphere `{z : ||z||_∞ = r}` has exactly `(2r+1)^3 − (2r−1)^3 =
  3499	   113	24r^2 + 2` points (gated by enumeration at `r = 1, 2, 3`: 26, 98,
  3500	   114	218).
  3501	   115	
  3502	   116	**Activity bound (the feed).** For the block07 activity with the `l_1`
  3503	   117	ambient diameter, grouping the pair sum by `l_∞` shells and using the
  3504	   118	conversion:
  3505	   119	
  3506	   120	> `κ ≤ K + sup_x Σ_{y≠x} ||h_{xy}|| · 2 · e^{mu||x−y||_1}`
  3507	   121	> `≤ K + 4K Σ_{r≥1} (24r^2 + 2) x^r`,  `x := e^{−(gamma_CT − 3mu)}`,
  3508	   122	
  3509	   123	(the `4 = 2 × 2`: the Hermitian-pair norm bound times `|S| = 2`), and
  3510	   124	with the exact numerator identity
  3511	   125	`24x(1+x) + 2x(1−x)^2 = 26x + 20x^2 + 2x^3 = 2x(13 + 10x + x^2)`
  3512	   126	(gated symbolically),
  3513	   127	
  3514	   128	> `κ_U ≤ κ̄ := K + 8K · x(13 + 10x + x^2)/(1 − x)^3`,
  3515	   129	
  3516	   130	finite for every `mu < gamma_CT/3` (`x < 1`), where `κ_U` is the true
  3517	   131	activity of the background-`U` family and `κ̄` is the **common
  3518	   132	envelope**. At `x = 1/2` the envelope evaluates to exactly
  3519	   133	`κ̄/K = 585` (gated by a derived closed form plus a
  3520	   134	partial-sum-and-tail bracket); the envelope carries deliberate slack —
  3521	   135	for a scalar fiber the exact pair norm is `|k|`, not `2|k|`, so the
  3522	   136	sharper scalar bound is `1 + 2·146 = 293` (also gated) — `585` is the
  3523	   137	value of the stated envelope, not of `κ_U`. Because `κ̄` depends on
  3524	   138	the background only through `K` and `gamma_CT` — which the CT note
  3525	   139	supplies as `U`-independent — the envelope is
  3526	   140	**background-independent**.
  3527	   141	
  3528	   142	**Theorem (fixed-background many-body LR for the gauged bilinear
  3529	   143	generator).** For every fixed background `U`, the second-quantized
  3530	   144	family above lies in the block07 weighted quasilocal class with the
  3531	   145	`κ` bound displayed, so the block07 theorem applies verbatim: for
  3532	   146	disjoint `X`, `Y` and all `t`,
  3533	   147	
  3534	   148	> `||[τ_t^{U}(A), B]|| ≤ ||[A, B]|| + 2||A|| ||B|| (n_X^w(U)/κ_U) ·
  3535	   149	> e^{−mu d} · (e^{2κ_U|t|} − 1)`
  3536	   150	> `≤ ||[A, B]|| + 2||A|| ||B|| |X| · e^{−mu d} · (e^{2κ̄|t|} − 1)`,
  3537	   151	
  3538	   152	the first line with the background's own constants, the second — the
  3539	   153	genuinely **uniform corollary** — with the single envelope `κ̄` and
  3540	   154	the coarse prefactor `|X|` shared by every background (the zeroth term
  3541	   155	vanishing when either observable is even, per the block04
  3542	   156	convention). This takes the **fixed-background half** of the CT
  3543	   157	note's open item (iii); the `mu < gamma_CT/3` threshold is the
  3544	   158	`d = 3` instance of the landed free-bilinear pattern
  3545	   159	`0 < d·mu < eta` (needled), and the `U = 1` scalar specialization recovers the same
  3546	   160	scalar-bilinear applicability pattern as the landed free-bilinear
  3547	   161	note (comparator; carrier conventions differ in detail and no
  3548	   162	carrier match is claimed).
  3549	   163	
  3550	   164	**Background-uniformity exhibit (exact, exhaustively enumerated).** On
  3551	   165	a 3-site chain with the toy `Z_2`-background kernel
  3552	   166	`h[s]_{xy} = s_{xy}·(1/2)^{|x−y|}` (`s_{xy} = s_{yx} ∈ {±1}`,
  3553	   167	`s_{xx} = 1`): all `2^3 = 8` sign backgrounds give identical pair
  3554	   168	norms `|h[s]_{xy}| = (1/2)^{|x−y|}`, hence identical activity — gated
  3555	   169	by full enumeration over backgrounds, with the box activity computed
  3556	   170	exactly at `e^{mu} = 9/8` under the note's envelope convention
  3557	   171	`||h_{xy}|| ≤ 2|k|` (the exact single-pair norm is `|k|`; using the
  3558	   172	envelope consistently makes the exhibit match the theorem's
  3559	   173	bookkeeping) (in one dimension `l_1 = l_∞`, so the
  3560	   174	exhibit incurs no conversion loss — stated, not hidden). The exhibit
  3561	   175	shows concretely what the uniformity claim uses: only the
  3562	   176	background-independent envelope of the kernel, never its signs.

import itertools
import numpy as np

# Independent occupation-bit implementation, not the runner's JW/Kronecker path.
def ann(j, n):
    d = 1 << n
    A = np.zeros((d, d), dtype=complex)
    for state in range(d):
        if (state >> j) & 1:
            lower = state & ((1 << j) - 1)
            sign = -1 if lower.bit_count() % 2 else 1
            A[state "'^ (1 << j), state] = sign
    return A

def pair(K):
    nf = K.shape[0]
    c = [ann(j, 2*nf) for j in range(2*nf)]
    T = sum(K[a,b] * c[a].conj().T @ c[nf+b]
            for a in range(nf) for b in range(nf))
    return T + T.conj().T

def onsite(K):
    nf = K.shape[0]
    c = [ann(j, nf) for j in range(nf)]
    return sum(K[a,b] * c[a].conj().T @ c[b]
               for a in range(nf) for b in range(nf))

w = np.exp(2j*np.pi/3)
